When it comes to the nodes, I largely agree; while I'd have preferred they provide a text language from the start, their node based system could definitely use a lot of the same features commonly found in text languages (structs, function definitions, etc.) My only quibble would be with #2; node based languages naturally lean toward a functional paradigm, and in such paradigms the actual order of execution doesn't particularly matter as long as you get the correct answer at the end.  The only reason to even have the execution flow at all is either for control flow, or because of timing.

(Wow, Canny's comment editing leaves a lot to be desired...)

With the VM, yes, I agree it's complicated, but I think in the long run, if it's implemented correctly (big if) it could actually represent a simplification of the overall program. (I've definitely experienced that firsthand in my own work.)

@{5b93e4741e75674a7ea03e2f|full_name}: 
"Those are all abstractions."
I agree that structures are completely abstract and irrelevant to bytecode, but arithmetic is neither abstract nor irrelevant. Efficient iterators and arrays (particularly safe arrays) require mathematics to be fast. Maybe you were thinking of arithmetic from the point of view of C#, where you can perform it on non-primitives and is therefore often very abstract.

"It doesn't matter (for the most part) if the IL uses three opcodes to add two numbers, or thirty."
The opcode parser would be O(1) complexity, so I'm not sure why you think something taking 10x longer doesn't matter. Though I think I get what you're really trying to get across when it comes to more abstracts ops that have a longer running time than opcode parsing (ie. CISC ops). With a RISC op, the time it takes to process that op in bytecode should be nearly as long running the op itself. This what the RISC arch endeavors to accomplish.

So comparing an ADD op to what UdonVM must currently do, it would be 4 ops (3 pushes + extern) vs 1. This would be a 4x increase in the time to complete. Which you could argue is 4x an insignificant number (nanoseconds maybe), but if it really is so arbitrary a choice as you suggest why would you choose 1/4 performance?

Because I'm assuming that the UIL is ultimately going to be compiled in some fashion.  Yeah there's a UdonVM interpreter, but that's quite likely to be just for testing. It might be just for the editor's sake; or maybe it does run on that right now... But this is an alpha.

It is important to remember that in a compiled environment, 2x opcodes does not necessarily mean 2x slower; and 1/2x opcodes does not necessarily mean 2x faster.  The UIL opcodes can be used to build an expression tree; that tree can be optimized, and the resulting tree be compiled. That's how many modern compilers work, especially with IL languages (.NET, Java, etc).

And the time to compile is not particularly important either; once it's compiled, it's compiled.  It's time to run that's important.

(And, BTW, an add in CIL could also potentially take 4 ops.)

Don't get me wrong; I'm not saying that UIL couldn't benefit from more opcodes (I myself would like to see more stack manipulation opcodes, for a start).  I am saying that I can't think of any opcodes that it absolutely must have in order to work, and that getting hung up on the number of opcodes it takes to express an operation is, at this early stage, indicative of premature optimization and should probably be avoided.
Ok, cancel all of that.  I didn't know about IL2CPP, and that apparently JITing isn't just not being done because alpha, but because impossible.

I too am dismayed by how low level this is despite being superficially a graph-based language. I’d almost go to the point of saying that it isn’t a graph-based language at all, but just a different and more annoying way to write C# code.

Do you think we could make a compiler which just takes C# and outputs the required unity asset for an Udon graph? ;D

I mostly agree about complexity of udon, too complicated for newbies, too weird for programmers. Like you even need to cast int to float manually with separate block.

And i somehow agree with most of other points but... allowing raw assemblies would be much much harder. They would still probably need to abstract half of unity engine to not allow any changes to selected components of the scene that could break the game, and you can't check that using static analysis, so it would need to check each method call or build second copy of scene with own types and only safe to work with objects. 
So the vm is the right choice, but sadly due to il2cpp they can't easily compile it to IL and just make the JIT do the job. They could only compile scripts on their own servers, but that could be expensive at large scale.
So imho we either need better VM support for custom types and other more advanced operations or for more ways to access byte arrays/memory would help a lot.

I agree, it's too complex for beginners without Unity & C# experience but too messy for complex programs. The graphs turn into spaghetti quickly and can even start lagging. I hope someone makes a text based compiler for Udon.

VM's are absolutely necessary when you have arbitrary execution and memory allocation capabilities. Udon's graphing system is not necessary to create such a VM. Labview has a big graphing language thats made to largely replicate standard programming languages and does so pretty well - but it's not as a safe VM afaik. Space engineers uses a 'safe' C# scripting system in game, however its actual safety may be dubious. Instead if there more mature secular webassembly (wasm) runtimes I'd advocate for that. 
To my knowledge with a proper wasm runtime you have memory and execution space safety guarantees from both how the instruction set is structured and from the runtime as long as it follows the standard. It would be possible to compile C# into modules that are controlled by the runtimes inherent VM. The control offered by this is complete, you can control down to the instruction, so you can throttle execution, limit memory, etc.
wasm is designed for interopability meaning only the chosen functions are exposed, and a layer can be implimented between for validation of any potentially dangerous usages of .net or unity functions. 

Having access to an actual programming language solves a number of use cases that cannot be predicted and accounted for - they're designed with open capabilities. Most unity development uses C# directly, with most of the tutorials and work done in it. 

With a graphing system you have a long list of things to re-impliment, and the output will still not be what anyone wants. But I can see why they chose to do it, there's a number of programs in this space that do it including Blender, Unreal Engine, CryEngine, etc. It's not a bad idea as long as VRCSDK2 stays around for normal users, and udons features are continually developed.

@{5e168b82752fbd5fe163b021|full_name}: simpler would be to just use Lua, its already highly adopted language in game dev with all features you need for it, and with separate JIT compiler when extra performance is needed.

@{5a4aaf7f758fa46d131cd36b|full_name}: Lua does not have the same level of safety guarantees. The environment around it is also outdated sadly. Lua has been a good choice for game mods, which were already mostly trusted.

@{5e168b82752fbd5fe163b021|full_name}: But its still fairly easy to create simple sandboxed environment in lua with only defined set of possible operations, and its already ready to use solution with a lot of tooling available. You don't need to implement near anything to add lua in safe way to your game. I would not be surprised if there is even a ready to use unity asset that does exactly this.

comments.body: I disagree with the suggested solution. You should be able to merge nodes regardless of adding new output flows. Having more output flows as a workaround is more complex and should be unnecessary. The flow of execution is not ambiguous, a branch can either go one way, or the other. This is already proven to be possible as other node based scripting languages in Unity already support it without custom output nodes. I have created an example image from Bolt and included it below:

I also disagree with this. Having an exit flow just adds more clutter and hurts the simplicity of the branch node.  I could see this being handy in some circumstances, but I think it would make the graph a bit hard to read. It just gives the branch too many responsibilities (evaluate bool, then choose direction, vs evaluate bool, choose direction, and then come back and take a different route).  I know the loop has an exit route, but that needs to be there for the loop to be effective.  Here, not so much.

Since February 23 you can now merge execution paths in Udon, except all nodes after the merge point end up duplicated in the resulting assembly. Other node based scripting solutions such as Bolt and uNode also have this problem, all nodes after the merge point show up twice in their respective C# preview.
Having a third output flow for Branch nodes would allow for smaller cleaner output and imho would not be clutter or overly complex. Both uNode and Nottorus handle their If nodes with a third output called "Finished"
You can now merge flows without needing this, assuming we can consider this closed.

The main concern here is that just Udon itself throwing a single error will spam logs without the user knowing. Resulting in some outrageous output log file sizes and what I presume to be constant writing to the drive.
As a quick experiment to see if this was possible to be malicious with, I was able to create a world with a single Udon graph that silently produces roughly 10MB of log spam a second. Also if you don't want a silent approach you can easily get upwards of 40MB a second but that is more likely to be noticed by the player as performance hitching.
An appropriate fix might be to throw an error then disable the offending script. If that breaks other Udon scripts they can just follow suit as the first error is what anyone debugging should look at.
An alternate fix idea might be to give the client the ability to enable Udon logging so that only creators should turn it on when they are debugging their worlds in game. That would avoid the average user from getting hit with this issue.

Trying to convert a Char to a float will always throw an InvalidCastException (as stated in the official microsoft .NET/C# documentaiton):

comments.body:
Thank you, although previously already reported. Please upvote those as well, missing modulo is truly a pain!

https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/missing-basic-math-functions-for-integers

https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/need-systemmath-unityenginemathf-is-not-enough-especially-remainder-operators
Ah thank you, this didn't show up for me when searching modulus

I’d almost say that remainder should be a second output from the division operation... but then modulo/modulus and remainder from a division aren’t the same thing if the thing you’re dividing is negative, so that adds hurt.
This was added in UDONSDK-2020.01.14.10.47_Public, however, it does not show up on the list anywhere
This has been added, but it is called "remainder".

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: I've searched as well as numerous other people and none of us can find "remainder" in the list of nodes we can add. This is with Udon version `UDONSDK-2020.01.14.10.47_Public`
@{5adf7c5544b24b6ef7cb0f25|full_name}: Hmm, gotcha. We'll take another look.

This has been partially resolved for a while, but modulus is only defined for for the following types: `float`, `double`, `decimal`, and `int`. There is a related canny for adding the remaining types: https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/long-remainder 
At the moment we're still missing modulus for the following types: `byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, `ushort`, `uint`, `long`, and `ulong`. Of these types, the currently exposed nodes cannot trivially represent modulus operations on `uint`, `long`, and `ulong` since their bit depth is larger than what the currently exposed modulus nodes can use.

Get what instance type you are in. Public, Friends, Friends+, Invite+, Invite
Single node can return string
Multiple nodes for each type can return bool
title: [Request] Instance Type node(s)

comments.body:
I'd really love to have this. It's a design thing. I'd use this to improve user experience.
For example, I'd be much more willing to grant global world controls to users in a private instance. Things like music toggles, atmosphere controls, etc. I wouldn't want to give that power to people in public instances, but I want to be able to give users control of their experience while maintaining a shared experience.
I'd be just as happy if a single node returned an integer index, but that's a design question :-)

I would be a little concerned with this about what happens if new instance types are introduced in the future. It might be better to structure this as a boolean private/public distinction (with f+ being public - since theoretically the set of people who can join is unbounded).

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: That is true and just getting whether or not the instance is public or private would be good. 
There is still the case where someone wants to be able to tell the difference between Public and Friends/Invite instances, so one could lock down things in a Public world while keeping it open in friends/invite instances
@{5a7ac88bf5a5c52c08064fb9|full_name}: yeah, I'm just wondering if this will have forward compatibility issues if eg group or group+ instances get introduced in the future.

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: fair point, not really something that was thought about at the time.
Either way, any of these options would be nice to have at least :)

This sounds great. (Though I'd consider f+ private)
In my worlds, I want to let players tailor the experience to suit their needs. But I **can't** do that, because a random player might join and press *all the buttons,* ruining the experience for everyone.
I could... introduce a passcode system? Or add a whitelist for whom I trust? But that just seems sub-par.
Being able to detect whether an instance is public would solve this issue. We would be able to give players more control, without compromising on the experience of publics.
I think this is a duplicate of https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/request-instance-type-nodes, which is tracked internally

comments.body: This can be fixed by making sure that you don't pull variables from branches that may or may not execute. In this case, the gameobject get transform node happens in the first branch, and then all the other branches pull from that. If it is separated so each branch has it's own gameobject get transform node, then it works just fine.

details:
We all know that Udon Programs in instantiated prefabs are strange... but I've found something related that it's not reported yet.
It seems that Udon can't compile correctly if there are no instance of the program while in EditMode.
I've linked a video showing the issue: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xJpP1QdFbzY
As you can see the instanced prefab Udon program do not gets updated (or compiled at all) until I instance the prefab in to the scene while in Edit Mode.
After the prefab is instanced in Edit Mode and you hit Play you can clearly see two different compiled programs running together.
The second time you enter PlayMode the prefab instance is updated with the correct version of the compiled Program (Probably, exiting PlayMode will cause some kind of refresh that actually end up updating the prefab instances with the updated program (?))
So... that's all, a workaround to ignore this issue until it gets fixed is keeping an instance of the prefab in to the scene ;D

details: I can see an issue on the horizon with Udon using nothing but programming terminology for it's node system. If the system is going to be user friendly and receive wide adoption it's going to need a major overhaul in the naming convention to more layman's terms. Or compromise with a toggle that labels nodes in an advanced or basic settings for those who wish to choose.
title: Amateur Friendly

comments.body: @{5ca510162225c760a69dd9a3|full_name} I'd be curious to know what terms would be easier for you.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: Sure! I mulled over a few terms that might be more easily understand by your average user. 
Boolean: Probably better visualized as Switch given it's on/off; yes/no behavior. I don't think I ever heard this term before learning some basic C#. 
Float: Another term I never heard until learning some programming. Might be better understood as a Decimal Number or a Number Fraction. 
Int/Integer: People might understand that this refers to a number, but it might be clearer if stated as a Whole Number. 
Block: I would have never guessed that a Block is what would let me distribute the same command to other nodes. To me a block is a thing that halts or stops something. I think Redirect or Distribute would illustrate that better.
I haven't constructed something in Udon needing For or While loops yet, but here's some possible alternatives that's clearer from the start.
For: Though okay, I think Duration or For Duration would get the point across quicker. 
While: I'm not sure what could replace this at the moment as it's okay as a term, but still not totally clear from the first look what it's for. In addition, I got a glimpse of this node and don't think any average person will understand what "Body" is supposed to denote as one of the branches out. 
This all of course could use a ton of workshopping and there is likely a ton of other properties that could stand further clarification, but it's what I've mused over at the moment.

@{5ca510162225c760a69dd9a3|full_name}: 
Nothing in a programming environment is going to be easy for people who don't know anything about it.
But most of these renames will, as I see it, just cause more confusion as they collide with other names or make it sound like it means something else.
I can see why Block can probably be confusing, but the other renames will cause even more confusion as they collide with other names that already exists in C#.
The best bet is to just get a really basic understanding of what these things mean.
I.e For loops, if that is renamed to Duration (which makes it sound like it's based on time/clock) will just make it even more difficult to read up on and understand. Since it doesn't match up with anything and would show you a result that doesn't have anything to do with it.

@{5ca510162225c760a69dd9a3|full_name} - thanks for listing out your ideas - as a programmer, it's helpful to understand what terms might trip up those with less programming experience.
I think it's important to learn some basic programming terms if you want to write programs - I think a lot of programming is just figuring out how to break problems down into smaller parts until you can solve each of those parts. Learning how loops work is fundamental to solving many problems - if you can describe your problem as a set of items that need to be processed, then you know you can use one of these tools to solve it!
It sounds like it would be helpful to have documentation (video,article,etc) describing the building blocks and what some of these terms mean. A big advantage in learning these terms is that they're pretty universal in programming - booleans, floats, ints, loops - these are found everywhere and will help you understand all sorts of code.
I agree with you about the Block node - it's specific to node-based programming and to Udon in particular, and there may be a better name for it, or at least some solid examples showing how it works.
We'll be rolling out tutorial videos to help, and the upcoming SubProgram system will enable the creation of more beginner-friendly nodes.

details:
All Unity types that inherit from Component have specialized GetComponent<T> functions for them that return the correct type of component directly or correct array type in the case of GetComponents<T>(). The signature for getting all components of type Transform is UnityEngineTransform.__GetComponents__TArray, this returns a Transform array.
This is very useful behavior since it means we don't need to convert array types ourselves, but UdonBehaviour does not define any of these specializations so we can't use the specialized versions on it and need to do regular GetComponent(typeof(UdonBehaviour)) which returns a type of Component or Component[] for GetComponents.
It would be nice to have these specializations for UdonBehaviours as well.
title: UdonBehaviour specialized GetComponent(s)<T> functions are not defined

details:
Currently the COPY instruction will automatically change the IStrongBox internal type for a heap variable if you attempt to assign a type that does not match exactly. This works well for a language that's weakly typed, but for strongly typed languages like C# this has a few problems that can break conventions in weird ways for the user.
What this means in effect is that there is no explicit casting between types in UdonVM as-is. We cannot tell it to turn a specific type into another. This has a few issues and limitations that come with it. So it would be nice to have an UdonVM instruction that force assigns a value to a heap strongbox value without changing the strongbox type and throws a runtime exception on failure to assign the type. 


Here's a few specific limitations we've run into so far:
a. System.Convert works a majority of the time for numeric conversions, but there are cases where it doesn’t behave the same as the dedicated CIL cast instructions. For instance, System.Convert does not support directly converting `char` to `float` whereas `Debug.Log((float)’a’)` is perfectly valid C# since the CIL instructions handle the cast properly. https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/convert-to-float-exception-when-converting-char-to-float 
b. You can cast integers to enums in C# `(HumanBodyBones)18` will give the enum value for HumanBodyBones.RightHand for instance. This is commonly used to iterate over all values of an enum. In Udon without special functions to emulate this behaviour https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/provide-enum-constructor-that-takes-an-integer-and-converts-it-to-an-enum-of-the , I don’t believe it’s currently possible to cast from int to enum. 
c. The biggest issue IMO is that there is no decent way to check that a class is a subclass of a specific type. It’s currently totally valid to copy a Vector3 into a heap variable that’s declared as a Renderer. Any code that references that heap value from that point on will treat it as a Vector3 and if any functions expect it to be a Renderer, they will break when they try to treat it as a Renderer. This can happen far down the execution chain from where the variable is set and can become more difficult to debug as a result. This can be emulated on the compiler’s side if we had access to more of the System.Type methods https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/expose-systemtypeissubclassof-isinstanceoftype-issubclassof-and-basetype but it would still be more performant to be able to tell the VM to do the cast and checking on its side. Exposing more of System.Type would still be useful for non-throwing type checking like the `is` and `as` operators https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/is-operator-with-possible-type-cast , but having a dedicated instruction that throws an exception on invalid cast would be nice for non-value types at least. 
For the class cast checks it should be enough to implement a generic function on the `StrongBox<T>` that takes an object and does `Value = (T)object;` on it. 
For the value type casts, it may require more complex handling since while the CIL instructions are somewhat generalized, I’m not sure how involved complex it would be to use C# primitives for generic casts. The best handling might just be to generate methods that actually do the casts from type to type based on what the CIL instructions for casting allow. In that case it’d be reasonable for me to add handling for those casts. For enum casts, I’ve just seen the CIL copy the int value straight into the enum variable. I don’t know if there’s a way to do that with just C#. Maybe the above linked suggestion of cast constructors for int to enum<T> would be the best. 
I’m not sure what the best course of action on implementing an instruction like this for value types would be, but it would be nice to have for reference types at the very least.
title: Provide an instruction that does not automatically reassign the strongbox type when source and target types differ

details:
If you use GetProgramVariable on an UdonBehaviour immediately after it has been initialized via VRCInstantate.Instantiate, it will return null for valid variable names since the heap has not been initialized yet. In order for the heap to be valid you need to wait for the UdonBehaviour's first update for the variables to be valid. Another case where GetProgramVariable will fail is if the UdonBehaviour is disabled and has never been enabled.
In a similar vein, if you set any heap variable via SetProgramVariable() before its heap has had a chance to initialize, SetProgramVariable will silently fail and any attempts to get the variable via GetProgramVariable() before initialization after setting it will return null.
SendCustomEvent also fails in a similar way https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/sendcustomevent-fails-on-gameobjects-that-where-instantiated-in-the-same-functio
It would be good if these functions (SetProgramVariable, GetProgramVariable, and SendCustomEvent, along with possibly SendCustomNetworkEvent) would force the UdonBehaviour to initialize itself if it hasn't already been initialized before they execute any logic. Right now it's unexpected behavior for people who instantiate game objects; I've seen a number of people run into issues with this already and need to work around it by delaying initializing the instantiated object by a frame which gets messy very quickly and requires them to register an Update function in cases where they may not need to otherwise or they need to move their initialization logic that depends on the initializer into the initializee which means they have a difficult time determining what behaviour instantiated them. It will probably also be confusing if people try to interact with a disabled component.
title: [588] Heap values are not initialized in some cases so GetProgramVariable() returns null when it shouldn't and SetProgramVariable() doesn't work

comments.body: Thanks for the in-depth report, @{5b07745b55c49e65e1c522d7|full_name}. We're looking at several issues around VRCInstantiate, this will be a helpful test as we fix up that node.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: Just wanted to make sure this was clear, it's also an issue on disabled UdonBehaviours that have never been enabled, not just VRCInstantiated behaviours. This has been a point of confusion for people because GetComponent<T>() on UdonBehaviours in U# needs the heap to be initialized on UdonBehaviours to work correctly.

details:
As Udon catches on and more people start using it, people will want to be able to localize their worlds, this includes such things as printing dates differently, offering a language select, or even getting the primary language of the user.
As it is currently, operations as simple as printing out the date, or a schedule for an event are difficult to do with no way to specify a region format to stick with, since the exposed ToString() method will only print out in the system language unless presented with an alternate locale, which we do not have the available methods to retrieve, as dates printed in an American format with swedish words for the month and day of the week will be quite awkward.
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.globalization.cultureinfo?view=netframework-4.8
This request is for all the functions and properties required to at least look up a locale if not to get the system locale so any Udon world can be localized.  They are listed below:
Properties:
DateTimeFormat
EnglishName
NativeName
Name
NumberFormat
Functions:
GetCultureInfo
GetFormat
Optional Properties:
CurrentCulture
CurrentUICulture
InstalledUICulture
UseUserOverride
title: System.Globalization.CultureInfo

comments.body:
A example of why this would need needed.
Language for the canvas is in English, but the date names are in Norwegian. Making this not look right.

Unable to parse into numbers because of this issue. 
Cultureinfo.invariantculture or similar needs to be passed to number converters like System.Number.ParseSingle

+1 to the replies below, have to parse as string as split it manually and then add it as a decimal and non-decimal part. Otherwise for people on French locale `float.Parse` will crash the udon behaviour completely if `.` is used as a delimiter. While using `,` will make it so it parses `1,75` as `175` which makes all the timings wrong.
This is really needed.
Some parts of CultureInfo have been exposed to Udon in the 2021.1.1 open beta.
Some parts of CultureInfo included in VRCSDK3-WORLD-2021.01.19.07.28

details:
Add a UnityWebRequest (HTTP GET) equivalent function set
tl;dr: Persistence and web connectivity IS going to happen whether these Udon functions are added or not, but it would be better to have a controlled, standardized, and built-in solution than the SDK2 style hacks that creators will standardize themselves.
For a long time world creators have done without web panels and have had to use VRC_Panoramas and shaders to squeeze out the smallest possible web functionality available (see Maki's clock prefab) in VRChat worlds.  With Udon's full programming power, world creators are finally able to make web based features for worlds - the main one being persistent values/settings across the whole platform.  Web connections can currently (almost) be done with SDK2-style workarounds instead of built-in Udon HTTP functions - which by all means SHOULD exist.  Creators have already altered the VRC_Panorama server system to return data directly through images, which can then be processed through Texture2D functions in Udon.  Creators have even set up video player based streaming servers that return similar data, in case a VRC_Panorama equivalent never resurfaces.  I've even personally planned for an external program that reads the game's output log, makes web requests through signals in the log, and returns data through OSC to make Udon web connectivity possible (though this is a sketchy and insecure solution, it would work better than other methods).  
The point here is that web connectivity IS going to happen whether these Udon functions are added or not, but it would be better to have a standardized built-in solution than the SDK2 style hacks that creators will standardize themselves.
There are 3 main arguments I've heard from VRChat staff against web functionality in Udon: sandbox security, user identity/IP protection, and the desire for an in-house persistence solution without the need for web connectivity.
The security of the Udon sandbox is not something that should keep this functionality from existing.  Simple HTTP requests do not allow for XSS style attacks, and there's no way simple data from an external server could harm the Udon VM, if the VM itself is secure.  Even if there were vulnerabilities in the Udon VM, they would be attack vectors that that don't even require web connectivity.  Plus, its already been established that people are going to make their own web request solutions.  If anything it would be LESS secure to not make HTTP requests available through Udon so security flaws could be easily patched in the future without breaking content.
Player IP protection is something that cannot be done. As Tupper has mentioned in a previous canny post, "IPs are not expected to be private information. ... If you want to keep your IP truly safe, we encourage the use of a VPN."  (https://vrchat.canny.io/bug-reports/p/eu-gdpr-compliant-serious-post-ip-grabbing) Completely protecting players' IP addresses would mean completely locking the game out from the outside world and removing features like video players and VRC_Panorama entirely.  Even now, you can go into a public world with a video player, drop in a link to your web server, and get the IP address of all users in the room.  Unless web based media is completely removed from the game, IP addresses are not going to be protected.
An in-house data storage/persistence solution for VRChat worlds is no real argument for limiting web connectivity at all.  Not everything people want to do with HTTP requests involves world persistence.  One use case might involve streaming in realtime data from a website to visualize in a VRChat world - something that's already done with VRC_Panorama except in image form.  A simplified persistence service provided VRChat could exist in the future for less technically inclined world creators, but it is by no means equivalent to full web connectivity.
Again, web requests are going to happen whether the VRChat team approves of its methods or not.  With the fine-grained level of control Udon provides, web requests will happen through inane workarounds that then go on to become established standards.  Please take control of this situation while you can and add an Udon Web API.
title: VRChat Udon Web API

comments.body: It's funny how we are using GET-requests with video players today to send all kind of data to a webserver, which processes it, turns it into a POST-request and also load data from the server back into another video player. Full web connectivity but an awful lot of overhead / performance.

The real question here is how to do it safely. Allowing anyone to access just any URL is quite big inherent security risk. How would you propose that be mitigated in a safe way? Because of this, I am 85% sure this will never become a reality, even though it would be quite nice.

@{5e6dd8bb6326616c1b8214e2|full_name}: in same way it was proposed long time ago by tupper, just display information on world and confirmation on first enter that given world is using some 3rd party services.
Additional security could be made by resolving url by vrchat hosted DNS + disallow any local ips to prevent people from trying to access anything locally.

I think the key problem with this is that VRChat content would break if the server not hosted by vrchat went away.
Yes web requests add allot of possible functionality, but you would inevitably end up with hundreds of Worlds that are broken and don't work.
This would be solveable with some sort of system where users clients report to vrchat when requests fail, and worlds get flagged as "Broken" but this would be overly exploitable. As for instance you could ddos a small server, or just block it on a couple machines and send hundreds of fake "webserver down" results to vrchat.
The argument about web players is flawed, because the easy fix for that, would be to whitelist domains that web players can access if they wanted to limit their security implications.
And the last bit about the fact that they will happen wether the vrchat team wants them or not, is wrong. They can be stopped if vrchat wants them to be, short of forcing all your players to use a modified client, you cannot gurantee a method of getting a webrequest out, as I mentioned above, vrchat can close the routes currently available, with fairly simple domain whitelisting.
Personally I would be all for web requests, I am msotly a web dev myself, and can think of many ways to use them, but they don't really outweigh the problems from vrchats perspective, if other forms of persistance / between world comunication were possible.
Also web requests will just lead to an awful lot of anti-user behaviour, we will get worlds that subscribe to shared "blacklists" to block people they don't like, tracking were users go, worlds that include some thrird party library to go some cool cars but include a backdoor to let the creator mess with any instance of your world tahts running.
I can't really see a good argument for web requests, so long as vrchat itself provides a decent persistence model, and some between instance comunication. Preferably persistence would have per user, per world, per group levels, but that's more something for a different issue.
Maybe outside api's could be made available on a case by case basis.

Related:
- [Waiting for VRC_Panorama replacement.](https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/waiting-for-vrcpanorama-replacement)
- [Add github​.com into Video Player Whitelist](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/add-githubcom-into-video-player-whitelist)
please also add websockets.

This would allow a lot of additional world richness which I think would offset the overall security risks. Almost every single device we have today spys on us, and consumers are generally OK with that. Heck lots of VRChat users already use the Quest 2, which is owned by a company whose whole business is based upon invading user privacy. 
I can tell you some of the really rich stuff I want to do with VRChat worlds involves accessing large data stores elsewhere. But even simple stuff like shared sculpting worlds are really hamstrung by the lack of network accessibility - how do you export your artwork?
A more restricted start would be allowing http connections to localhost, but that will ultimately result in someone simply building a proxy. 
My preference is that this work like permissions in android, the world creator needs to explicitly tick a box that says they wish to use networking, and then when a user views the world or enters the world the user is warned that this world accesses the network. I suspect this also will result in needing a more optimized UDON, or some simple restful helper functions. 
I am seriously considering creating worlds in other platforms if they let me have unrestricted HTTP access, I want to visualize a complex 3d data set which is petabytes in size and have the awesome features of VRChat.

If an interactive object is cloned with VRCInstantiate, both the cloned object and the original object will lose interactivity.

In the images below, the graphs ordered by when they were mentioned. The graph in the first image should be set to a gameobject #1 and the one in the second image should be set to gameobject #2. Then, the variable should be set to gameobject #1. Gameobject #1 should be a 3D cube (this is not necessary), and #2 should be an Empty (again, not necessary).

Other info:
This error only occurs on live worlds. Local testing works as expected (both objects are interactable). This can create very confusing errors and broken worlds.

Tested Version: VRCSDK3+UDON-2020.04.01.10.20.
title: Interactive Objects break after being cloned/instanciated on live worlds.

@{5e87c0a24b04267f0b960603|full_name}: This is more of a request to expose the standardized interpretations of those inputs, as setting up custom actions for every input becomes tedious as well as pointless as soon as people start rebinding their controls.

Was going to make my own post but found this one - here are my thoughts on how things are right now:
For a while we were able to get away with unity's input system - it was messy on Vive/wmr, but it worked for the most part once you had everything mapped out (the spreadsheet posted in another comment). If you used steamvr rebinding to put jump on your A button, it would send a joystick click and everything was fine. This is how things were when this post was first made.
But since the update to vrchat that allowed ingame rebinding, you can now rebind the A button to jump without it actually sending the joystick click. Udon has no way of knowing how the player's inputs are set up so it is impossible to accurately get the jump input, among other things.
At minimum, we need to be able to poll or receive events from the following inputs after they have gone through vrchat's controller specific interpretation, rebinding, and dead zones:
-Locomotion (x/y for smooth and a bool for holoport)
-Turning (single frame pulse of 1 or -1 for snap, or a regular axis for smooth)
-Jumping
-Grip buttons
-Trigger buttons
-Menu buttons
If it's possible it would be great to have the following extra Inputs:
-Currently active gesture for left/right hands
-All finger tracking axes
-Some extra actions that people can put wherever they want using the ingame rebinding
Available in build 1061: https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/input-events

details:
VRCSDK3+UDON-2020.04.03.13.19

If you tab away from the graph editor or change selection of objects in the hierarchy the graph editor desyncs from the assembly code it is tied to.  At this point any further changes you make to the graph do not result in any functional changes when the world is built and tested.  

Discovered this with just a simple script where a cube disabled another cube.  After testing the disable functionality I changed the script to be a enable/disable toggle, but the enable functionality never worked.  I destroyed and recreated the component with the full toggle capability from the start and it worked. details:
Using GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() is much slower than using GetComponent<Rigidbody>() for no particular reason. And using GetComponent(typeof(ScaleConstraint)) has better performance than the generic counterpart to the point that it's on par with the generic GetComponent<Rigidbody>().
The following tests were run using this script compiled with UdonSharp https://gist.github.com/Merlin-san/7b785bda752798115522010f8f3983c6
The baseline time to do 10,000 iterations on a loop in editor with the attached script is around 13.4ms on my computer. Enabling the generic GetComponent<Rigidbody>() call brings the loop time up to around 17.5ms which means the GetComponent<Rigidbody>() takes about 4.1ms to run 10,000 times in editor.
Enabling only the GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() brings the time to execute up to 19.5ms which means GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() takes about 6.1ms or 50% longer than GetComponent<Rigidbody>() for no reason.
Both GetComponent(typeof(Rigidbody)) and GetComponent(typeof(ScaleConstraint)) take about 4.4ms so there’s something wrong with the generic version of GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>(). In U# the generic version of this gets converted to an extern call to “UnityEngineAnimationsScaleConstraint.__GetComponent__T”.
Running the code as actual C# instead of U# on Udon, has the loop taking 0.04ms without any GetComponent calls. Using either GetComponent<Rigidbody>() or GetComponent<ScaleConstraint>() makes it take about 0.6ms on average. So there isn’t a disparity in performance on C#.
If the necessity for pushing the System.Type to the input arguments for the __GetComponent__T variants is removed when you look at this, it would be a welcome change since right now U# needs to redundantly push the System.Type of the component type you’re attempting to get despite every type having a specific function defined for it. Like in this case “UnityEngineAnimationsScaleConstraint.__GetComponent__T” should return a ScaleConstraint type and that’s already defined by the name of the method so we shouldn’t need to redundantly push the type. 
This canny may also be relevant: https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/getcomponentst-functions-are-not-defined-internally-for-vrcsdk3-components

edit:
Intentionally breaking the U# compiler to always call the extern "UnityEngineCollider.__GetComponent__T" no matter the type and pass in the correct System.Type for the requested type still works for any type. I'm able to get a ScaleConstraint type by pushing a System.Type of the ScaleConstraint type and calling the "UnityEngineCollider.__GetComponent__T" extern. Which indicates that the specialized GetComponent_T functions are probably doing a redundant lookup with a giant switch statement or something when they already should know what type they need to return since the return type is specified by the method extern signature in this case.
title: Performance disparity between GetComponent<T> on two different types

Still an issue as of build 946. Will now error in editor without the secure heap enabled when using the new SDK since the checks are done on each extern now.

Introducing a new Utilities.IsValid(object) method which does a few things internally, including safely checking whether a UnityObject.Equals(null).
@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: A proper fix is preferable, as otherwise holding a reference to a destroyed object is still vary dangerous to the lifetime of the script
@{5f2d19d0a2990547bfc05f3a|full_name}: you should be able to safely replace your null checks with .IsValid() checks.
Utilities.IsValid added in update 2021.1.3 https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrchat-202113

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: Utilities.IsValid is a work around, but not a solution. This canny is specifically asking about null equality operator throwing an exception when it should not. The defined behavior of Unity is still broken so this is not resolved.
Anyone coming to use Udon from normal Unity development will not know to use IsValid and will be confused by the guarantee that null equality is supposed to ensure being broken. Implementing proper work around handling from the compiler side would involve a dozen extern calls and several conditional jump instructions since on its own IsValid is a subset of the functionality of unityengine object equality/inequality.
Given Udon's performance characteristics that would mean an unacceptable performance hit in many use cases for something that should be handled properly as a single extern call since the unityengine.object equality/inequality/implicit boolean conversion methods are exposed.
sorry, shouldn't have been moved to complete yet, we understand the ask for null check to be fixed separate from IsValid.

comments.body: @{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name} Since the tracking data and human body bones have always been inconsistent between remote and local clients and for different avatars, and we now have fallback avatar IK syncing to remote clients with some kind of normalized bone rotations for the human body bones, hopefully we're in a good position to bring some consistency to this API. If the rotations used for displaying remote fallback avatars and stuff can be calculated both locally and remotely and then provided as the rotations in udon that wouldn't be a breaking change to the API and then we would have useful body bone rotations and it would be simple to fix tracking data orientations for the remote clients hands as well.

@{6010b37283e56405c64a79b3|full_name}: yes, this is something I've looked into quite a bit. It's not a trivial problem, because unity's humanoid bone system is a bit of a black box. fallbacks work by just applying the same "muscle" data to a different avatar, which results in a similar pose. But there isn't really a good way of directly taking that muscle data and turning it into a complete, standardized position/rotation unless you were to apply that muscle data to a standardized rig. 

It is possible to use reflection to reach into the unity black box and pull out information about the current rig and the rotations needed to provided a calibrated position, but reflection is a very messy, expensive method which could break with unity updates. It's appropriate for editor scripts but better to avoid in a built game.

Another method that I've personally explored is to perform a calibration every time an avatar is loaded while they're in a T-pose, and store a relative rotation that you'd need to get from the actual bone rotation to a standardized rotation. Then when udon asks for a standardized rotation, you combine the two together. The problem with this is that not all T-poses are equal. Some avatars have overridden their T-pose to be an A-pose or even I-pose, usually for the purposes of changing how you calibrate FBT. But for the purpose of standardized calibration, that screws things up quite a bit and it would not be trivial to jam in a whole new playable layer just for a new T-pose. Additionally, some avatars have really weird bones that makes it hard to build a good standard without reaching into the unity black box. I have spent some time mostly handling that, but the more you look the more exceptions you find.
@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: Ahhh drats, that's much more cursed than I thought it was.

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: You know, now that I think about it, I wonder if you could take the muscle data that is used for IK syncing and apply it to a standardized rig with the proportions matched to the avatar. Might be able to combine that with what you were trying to do: just load up the standard rig once during T pose, apply the same muscle positions to it that the T pose has, and then carry the offsets with the avatar. Although I don't know how the muscle positions and T pose and all that all relate so that is probably something you've looked into as well.

@{6010b37283e56405c64a79b3|full_name}: applying muscle data to a standardized rig is a lot to ask if you do it every frame for every player because you're just duplicating the amount of work, which is already quite expensive.

But only doing that once on calibration and saving the difference is a very good idea. It would completely avoid the issue of people having A or I poses, while also providing a much more "normal" standard rather than something homebrewed. I'll have to experiment with that some time to see if it would work.

Found this out myself today.  Put together a project with a bunch of assets I planned to use, took a couple minutes to build even though I barely had anything in the scene to do a quick test.
Put together two new projects to test what was going on, one with sdk2 another with sdk3.  Both were setup with only a plane and the corresponding world prefab.  With nothing else imported sdk2 took 2 seconds to enter play mode, sdk3 took 5 seconds.  Then imported a single asset pack but did not use it in the scene, sdk2 still took 2 seconds, sdk3 started taking near 30 seconds.

Please fix this, it takes minutes to get into playmode wtf -.-
Decided to load everything I had into a project to see how bad this gets...  project takes 10 minutes to get into play mode with an empty scene.  well then.

This happens because UdonEditorManager.PopulateAllPrefabSerializedProgramAssetReferences loads all prefabs and searches UdonBehaviour. Candidate files are gathered by UdonEditorManager.GetAllPrefabAssetPaths. That are actually "all prefabs". It is completely wasteful to load pre-existing assets that are not made for Udon or VRChat.

@{5cb0e62414ddd360bbe1ac29|full_name}: Unfortunately no, this just means Udon has to think about every asset in your project before it will let Unity go into Play mode. What you're probably running into is either from lots of audio of high lightbaking settings.
@{5bad030cf511392c4ddf27bc|full_name}: I figured out it's actually a bug with setting items to static batching. For some reason that feature is bugged at the moment and causes file size to skyrocket.

With what @{5a983204a1528d415c5ced46|full_name} stated, it is indeed that particular method that slows down the 'play' time, because of the unnecessary loading. Simply changing the folder path it needs to search in to something that has far less prefabs in it speeds up load times drastically (especially with projects using large amounts of prefabs).
I don't know the exact consequences in changing this, but I thought I'd share what happens upon doing so.

@{5a983204a1528d415c5ced46|full_name}: This method needs to be run but we'll look into making it more specific to avoid processing so many unused prefabs.
This method and much of how Udon is serialized is done specifically to work around a number of issues we encountered when dealing with Unity's Prefab and Asset systems. UdonBehaviours depend on a SerializedUdonProgram asset that contains the serialized data built from the UdonProgramSource asset. UdonBehaviours in the scene can easily be found and checked to make sure they have a valid reference to their SerializedUdonProgram asset. Prefabs on the other hand may not even exist in the scene if they are only referenced by a scene object. If a prefab loses its reference to the SerializedUdonProgram asset for its ProgramSource then it will fail to run. To avoid this prefabs are checked before the world is run or built to ensure that their references are valid. Unfortunately there is no way to know whether a prefab is "pre-existing" or "made for Udon" without checking for an UdonBehaviour.

Don't get why it's necessary to scan *all* prefabs? Why not to just scan prefabs referenced by scene, especially defined in VRCSceneDescriptor. In Play mode all prefabs unpacked anyways and things that can be instantiated should be defined in descriptor. Is there another way how UdonBehaviours in prefabs can get into running scene?
Also full-checks might be necessary when building final bundle for upload. But at editor-time we have acces to entire project anyways, so why not to check necessary UdonBehaviours at run-time and do necessary fixes in editor, where it's necessary?
My main project takes 15 minutes to enter play mode. So I cant test my scenes there basically. Would be appreciated if something can be done.
Running into the same issue here, i have over 3k prefabs and its taking longer that 5 min to enter play state.

This seems to be fixed now in a recent update (at least for me). My large project that took 15 mins to load now loads in about a minute. (I did have some issues regarding prefabs losing references to which udon script was attached to them upon first upgrading, but I'm not sure that's related.)
@{5e5961740ab4231b6f14d29c|full_name}: I can close this if you'd like, then.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: This one was really nasty for a lot of people, If possible I'd like at least one other confirmation from someone else to be 100% sure.

This was improved a while ago. There was a specific step in the process that scanned and serialized udonbehaviour variables. It could take multiple minutes in large scenes. It received multiple optimizations to reduce it down to about 5% of it's previous time.

details:
A deep profile of the udon VM in the engine shows a significant amount of time being spent in CheckExecutionTimeLimit. I suspect this is being called on each instruction. Since checking the high-resolution system timer can be very expensive (involving system calls, and/or a serializing RDTSC instruction), this should be avoided.
I would suggest two simple mitigations to help reduce this impact:
1. First, the execution time limit needs only be to be checked on loops - that is, on backwards branches - because otherwise, the program will eventually halt. Alternately, it could be checked every N instructions.
2. Second, the execution time limit could be checked using a less precise timer. There could be a second thread that, every second, increments a global atomic counter; the udon VM could read this counter and check against the value observed when execution began.
title: Reduce calls to CheckExecutionTimeLimit

details:
While trying to make a procedural generated map i encountered one fairly big problem when it came into syncing the generation.
When you use a seed to have the UnityEngine.Random object to generate the same values for everyone you can get the desired effect only in the current frame, from the successive frame onwards it will generate values differently from each other. My guess is that UnityEngine.Random is also used internally by vrc for other stuff, and that causes the internal state of the random generator to desync.
One solution would be to store the state of the number generator at the end of the frame and reset it at the start of the next frame, but that needs the UnityEngine.Random.State class to be exposed.
Another solution would be to Expose the System.Random class instead, since that class is not static and you can instance indepenent objects that would also avoid potential interference of UnityEngine.Random being set and reset by the user and then vrc using it internally for other reasons consequentently alterning the random generation.
title: Easier way to sync Random generators

details: RunProgram takes a uint address to start an event rather than a string event name. Right now to call methods on other behaviours, we must call SendCustomEvent which has overhead for looking up the target function's entry point in a behaviour. Exposing RunProgram would allow compilers to optimize method calls across behaviours more effectively by running a linking stage that finds the addresses of the target methods to avoid the runtime lookups of method names when possible.
title: Expose UdonBehaviour RunProgram

SDK: VRCSDK3-UDON-2020.04.25.13.00
UdonSharp_v0.15.9 (used for comparison only)
General Description:
I'm using a while loop to increment a  private variable which is to be used to Exit the loop. The exit condition is tested against a fixed value with an  "Op Less Than" node that feeds into the bool of the While node. Even though the variable value increments up past the fixed value, the (presumed) change in state of the "Op Less Than" does not cause the While node to take the Exit path.
For comparison, I repeated the program with UdonSharp. It works correctly as expected.
Files included:
Graph and UdonSharp snapshots are attached.
You can find assets for both the Graph and the UdonSharp versions here:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12RfzTi6IEFK3wPsA0_LO_NpHt8YxmkFA?usp=sharing
Step by step guide (failure):
1) Create new world, install SDK and UdonSharp.
2) Add a floor and a cube.
3) Add Box Collider and VRC Pickup to box.
4) Add Udon Behavior to cube and set Program Source to LoopTest.
5) Build & Test.
6) In game, interact with the cube.
7) Wait 10 seconds for program to timeout.
8) Look at the output_log. You will notice that variable TargetPlayer (an int) increments up without stopping until the timeout exception.
Ste by step guide (try UdonSharp):
9) Change the Udon Behavior on the cube to LoopTest_us.
10) Build & Test, and repeat interaction.
11) Look at the output_log. Notice that the loop ends and the last {LoopTest] log entry is an [Exit] message, indicating that the While loop has exited.
title: "While" node not comparing latest private values in bool condition.

details:
EDIT: I figured out the issue with the file size, it ended up being the way I was setting plants as static and unity just not liking it.

Original post:

Okay, so I decided to start using the SDK3 for making new worlds and decided to start with a simple home world. I made the place kind of big with lots of trees and plants and a house. The file size ended up a pretty standard 200 something MB. Performance wasn't great so I went back in and made the world smaller. The world had less stuff in it over all, but when I went to check it out, the performance was even worse and the file size had tripled to a whopping *600 MB.* I thought maybe I was putting to many trees in, so I made it even smaller, with far less objects in it. After uploading it the file size was now nearly 1,000 MB!! I didn't bother letting it load in. 
At this point I went and looked in the bug reports and some people were saying that Udon SDK3 scans all objects in the project at run time, and I wondered if that was the cause of the issue. So I decided to clean out anything I wasn't using from the project files in hopes of making it small again. This didn't really do anything as it stayed around the same file size even after crunching more textures.
So this time I decided to drastically reduce the amount of light probes by nearly half and I cleared out the dynamic objects and dynamic materials again because they had reset themselves. I rebaked the lightmaps and double checked I didn't have anything hidden in the map. This time I didn't even bother with a play test in Unity. Despite my best efforts, this only reduced the file size by about 9 MB, bringing it to a total of **939 MB.** My world is only a 200x200 terrain piece with a house. It shouldn't be this big. 
As a last resort, I uploaded the world again with a new blueprint ID, deleting the old version. This only reduced it to 918 MB. Once again I decided to reduce the amount of light probes. I rebaked the lighting. The file size stayed the same. At this point I have no idea what is causing the file size issues except maybe the SDK is uploading everything in the project and maybe more stuff that I'm not aware of, like maybe the GI cache?
TLDR: File size is like 10 times bigger than it should be and there's almost no way to reduce it.
title: [fixed] Udon Worlds are a HUGE file size!

details:
Now that web connectivity will likely require some form of consent from the user when using Udon, I think it's a reasonable request to ask for an actual unique user ID that we can use to identify users. This could be used to do things like enable a debug console in the world, or when web connectivity is back, save progress or settings in a world.
Right now people are using display names as "unique" identifiers which isn't good and already has issues since it's a display name. One issue is https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/onplayerjoined-doesnt-get-full-displayname-for-steam-users 
Another issue is that "special" characters like "." get replaced in the display name with lookalikes which breaks string comparisons. 

Relying on display name to "uniquely" identify people will become more prevalent as time goes on and people make commonly used systems that depend on them. You should expose this sooner rather than later to avoid this issue.

The potential for abuse is obviously possible, but there's no reason to kneecap the systems and introduce potential issues by leaving only display names visible. Right now I can reasonably target people with just their display names, it's just possible that there will be some more people with the same name that get targeted. Worlds abusing names to harass people is something that should be reported on a world basis.
title: Expose unique user IDs to Udon

comments.body:
I don't understand why the unique user ID isn't exposed to Udon. The unique user ID isn't secret, I can easily [use the VRChat website to get the unique user ID from the URL of any player](https://help.vrchat.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408181867027-Account-Names-and-Identifiers) I want.
Has VRChat devs given a reason for it not being available?
Support, no clue why this isn’t already a thing.
@{5b07745b55c49e65e1c522d7|full_name} Since you are internal now, can you campaign for this?

This is just a guess. But one of the reasons we don't have access to user IDs, might be because VRChat thinks it will limit the chance of people making blacklists.

See: [Udon Moderation Tool Guidelines](https://creators.vrchat.com/worlds/udon/udon-moderation-tool-guidelines/)

PS: Why is this document so hard to find? I could not find it before I knew it existed.
This seriously needs to be a thing, creating custom systems for worlds and only being able to use DisplayName is crazy when there is already a UUID available
It's insane this issue has still not been addressed after 5 years.  Being able to spoof whitelists by changing display name is starting to become a legitimate security concern.

So many maps are grossly insecure due to this, and most scripted moderation tools are incapable to deal with something as simple as a display name change.

I get the fear of people making ban lists, but there are already reporting functions for this, it isn't something that need to be solved on the technical side.

It even hinders the ability for games to keep track of players that leave the instance and rejoin.

If the VRChat team is worried about data-collection concerns from having a unique ID exposed between different worlds, or the creation of ID-based ban lists, there is an alternative solution:

Add a secondary private ID to all accounts (not exposed to the account owner either), and then the Worlds API can have a function to request "getWorldUniqueUserID()".

VRC central server would then respond with an ID that is generated based on that internal hidden private ID, plus the world ID, and a secret global key only VRC knows about.

This would provide an ID that remains consistent for each user in a per-world context, but would prevent reverse-engineering to expose any cross-world trackable information.

It would allow save files to be created in a world that can be both secure and still be restored even if a user completely resets their persistent data (or it gets corrupted). Only breaking if a world is deleted and uploads to a new World ID.

This would also not add any significant load on VRChat's servers, as it would only calculate it if the call is even made, and cache the result to prevent further calls.

-----------------------------------------------

Thinking further into the future, this system could be expanded by replacing the "world ID" part of the unique ID generation with a "shared world ID", allowing a set of worlds to have a secondary "shared ID" value if approved to be linked together. This way if some experiences need to be split across multiple worlds, they can still share the same per-world unique ID for the user. 

(But that is something that would have to be approved for linking to avoid large networks of linked worlds just to force shared IDs.)

World creators can already "blacklist" people based on their displaynames. If the reason this hasn't been implemented is the fear of blacklisting based on user ID instead, that could simply be reported if it's being abused. The more pressing security issue is obviously that worlds can't protect against spoofing at all without unique IDs! I would much rather let users have the IDs and deal with reporting the few world creators that abuse the system than leave every world/udon asset unprotected against the most basic displayname spoofing attack.

I've honestly been hoping for a feature like this for years.  The few times I've changed my display name has caused major havoc for all the venues I perform at.  Having to manually contact each of the world owners and have them update their whitelists is tedious at best.

Currently, there are the following assembly dependencies in the udon libraries: VRC.Udon.VM -> VRC.Udon.Wrapper -> UnityEngine.*
When developing compilers for udon, it would be helpful to be able to actually execute code against the udon VM without having to run in the unity editor. This could be achieved more easily if the wrappers were split into one assembly for .NET core classes and one for unity types, and allowing the VM to be instantiated using only the .NET core class wrappers.
title: Split Udon assemblies to allow for out-of-editor execution

[Steps to reproduce]
1. Lay out many (about 50 or more)  MonoBehaviour and  VRC_Pickup  objects in the scene.
2. Enter the world with 3 or more people.
3. All player pick up and move some objects.
4. Join a new player.
5. The coordinates of some objects are not synced correctly to the new player.
[Cause]
Maybe, ownership information is not correctly transmitted to new player.
In the new player, owner of some objects will appear to be the master.
But the owner is actually a different player.
So the coordinates by the true owner send to be ignored, the new player will see the object appear to be stationary from its initial position.
Also, if an object is picked up by the true owner of that one, SetOwner is not called.
So new players will continue to recognize that the master is the owner.
[Interim measures]
Always the master keep to hold all ownership of objects.
title: Owner information is not correctly synced to new players when there are many UdonBehaviour objects.

details:
Currently, Udon makes "security checks" on runtime, but instead of checking an array once, it checks each element of an array whenever you access _one_ element in that array, causing exponential execution times for even the smallest arrays.
This causes huge permance issues whenever you use arrays, forcing you to write super ugly code that works without them whenever possible.
But: This UdonVM behaviour makes no sense from a security perspective. When I _create_ and _fill_ an array in Udon on runtime of a known/whitelisted type (e.g. a Vector3), there is no need to check whether or not this array is still secure when I read from it again. UdonVM needs to check an UdonBehaviour _once_ for secure/whitelisted content, not every time it is run. The whole overhead of runtime security checks shouldn't exist in a VM that only supports a set of whitelisted components.
Right now, making more complex things in Udon that rely on running in Update() is especially frustrating because it always runs fine in the editor (as it should) while it runs on 1 fps in vrchat. And this is only because you need to loop once through a few local arrays of whitelisted components with 30 elements each.
The only workaround right now is to use hundreds of class variables instead of arrays to get your frametime back. The code is unreadable at this point and coding for VRChat becomes a pain.
title: Improve runtime performance for arrays

(speculative) reproduction:
1. Create udon behaviour that on Update(), calls `Networking.LocalPlayer.GetBonePosition(HumanBodyBones.LeftHand)`
2. Assign udon behaviour to gameObject that's active in scene by default
3. In game, observe that the UdonBehaviour sometimes crashes with an exception in the console, and other times works.
I think there's an initialization race condition with the VRCPlayerAPI, where the GetBonePosition call can throw an exception if executed too early in the scene.
A real example that helped a user was adding this line (in UdonSharp) to a script: https://github.com/hiinaspace/utheremin/blob/3022801f9c3b844ebc69a57879d9b495fd0f0036/Assets/UTheremin/HandFollower.cs#L46 , i.e. waiting 3 seconds after Start() was called before attempting to call GetBonePosition.
Unfortunately I couldn't reproduce locally, but the workaround does seem to work for the user that reported the issue.
title: VRCPlayerApi.GetBonePosition sometimes throws exception if called early in scene

> I think it is necessary to generate IL code dynamically in advance instead of using the interpreter.
This game is currently compiled using il2cpp, so at the end the game client is mostly native cpp. So its a lot more complicated. 
But the real question still should be: why did vrchat team decide to write own simple VM like that for udon.
As other alternative solutions:
- Use existing VM-s, like lua, on desktop lua-jit could be used. And udon graphs could be just compiled to it. Lua can be used in safe sandboxed mode with whitelist of available methods, so it would be safe and would be still easy and simple to disallow access to some components/objects on scene. Pros: there is shit tons of existing resources for lua, would make developing much easier and faster. Cons: Can't find a single one.
- Compile udon bytecode to native code on backend. Pros: could be made very fast. Cons: Hard to implement + cost.
- Compiling to IL should be also possible with some additional tricks... as c# runtime can talk with cpp code, but I have no idea if there are any existing tools for unity to create such mixed environment, with both il2cpp + additional code in pure c#/il.
As otherwise I dont believe that udon VM will ever get fast enough, as fast as other languages developed by much larger teams with a lot of experience.

@{5a4aaf7f758fa46d131cd36b|full_name}: I think that it is better to generate IL/native code by each clients before loading scene.
@{5dfdc395425b056c1932da3c|full_name}: well, that would be much more complicated, especially with il2cpp

details:
Since bone transforms aren't exposed, we can't parent objects to players and need to use expensive and complicated update loops for such a basic task, which also results in ugly/janky object movements and low performance. 
Please give us a simple function like .SetParent(Transform t, Boolean b) for .GetTrackingData(VRCPlayerApi.TrackingDataType.x) and .GetBonePosition(HumanBodyBones.x) and for VRCPlayerApi.GetPosition
title: Allow parenting objects to player bones, player position and player tracking data

comments.body:
+1, and I'm surprised that after a year there hasn't been any feedback on this yet. I've been trying to attach things to players with udon, and the syncing of things just isn't optimal, both client and server side.
Add to that the fact that bone rotation can be even more janky and a direct parent to the bones would honestly solve all of this jank.

If there are concerns about directly exposing player bones to Udon (where Udon scripts could potentially pose the player's avatar, for example), other options include e.g.:
1. Creating a proxy transform parented to the bone, and exposing that transform (only) to Udon (note that this risks destroying world objects on avatar unload, possibly this should reparent any children of the proxy to the scene root before unload)
2. Adding an API to link a constraint on a world object to a player bone transform

Any kind of function to create an exposed dummy object that is parented accordingly would be amazing. Any support for this would go a long way to enabling better hitboxes, custom HUDs, and one less hoop to jump through for some shader effects.

As is for OnPlayerEnterTrigger events, the local player has a full capsule, while non-local players seem to have a sphere that only goes up to their waist. There's a necessity to work around this with custom hitboxes for projectile collision, which raycasting is not always ideal for. Player based object parenting would go a long way to work around this, while also allowing for more flexibility with head, limb, and finger detection.

Please add this capability to VRChat/Udon/UdonSharp! It's been years of high performance Update() function demand for FPS related worlds that could be significantly cleaned up through more native support in Unity with child objects or constraints. Only one dummy object needs to exist (via a function for on-demand creation of them) for each of whatever bone or tracking item that is sought to tie things into.

details:
Thanks for checking out this new version of the Graph UI. You can install it using the link below - please do a CLEAN install - close Unity, delete your library and the existing Udon folders (Udon, VRChat Examples and VRCSDK) and then import the new package.
 
There's lots to see! Please take a look and file your findings - bugs, features and suggestions.

Feel free to upload and test things with this SDK, this should all work on Live with the provided SDK. 

Make sure to save your projects separately! New graphs should be mostly backwards-compatible, but no guarantees. The new Comments and Groups will not appear in the old Graph.
 
To open the New Graph, you can find it under VRChat SDK > New Graph or on an UdonBehaviour with the 'Open New Udon Graph' button. You can still access the old graph for now - this will be removed for public release.
Existing Udon bugs will not be any different, this is purely an upgrade to the Graph Window that should make it easier to use, and enable lots of great future upgrades (SubGraphs, etc). We want to test that existing graphs open and compile well with this UI, and that building new graphs works as expected. We're happy to hear about suggested features along with bugs.

SDK Link: https://files.vrchat.cloud/sdk/VRCSDK-UDON-2020.06.04.14.15_Closed_Community_Test.unitypackage
 
What's New:
 
New UI Elements

* Variables are part of a floating window now. You can create, rename and delete them right in this window (they will not show up as nodes). You can drag and drop from the window to your graph to create a 'Get Variable' node or use Search to get Set Variable nodes. We also use a text-matching search function when choosing variable types rather than the long list.
* Groups - create through right-click, drag-and-drop to add items inside.
* Comments - now standalone items created through right-click with adjustable size.

UI Improvements

* Zoom! Just roll your mousewheel!
* Visible Compilation state - check out the box in the upper-right of the graph screen. It will flash green when compiling successfully, and red when unsuccessful. Click on the box to show/hide the latest assembly or errors.
* Ports are easier to connect now
* Copy+Paste Improvements - new nodes appear around mouse
* Welcome screen for messages, known issues and settings
* Right-Click to add Nodes
* Alt+click to drag as well as middle-mouse
* Drag and Drop GameObjects from your Hierarchy to a graph to create a new Public Gameobject variable.
* New StyleSheet system - This is lower-priority, but you will be able to reskin the graph. You can see an example by turning on 'Use Neon Style' in the Settings, this will apply 'UdonGraphNeonStyle.uss' over the existing graph. Do poke around if you're curious. Don't spend time customizing this yet - we're likely to change the names and classes of some elements as part of cleanup so your custom styles will break. We'll let you know when this is locked and add an easy way to apply your own stylesheet.
 
Search
* There's now a few ways to search. Press spacebar to open up Quick Search, which will give you access to a few special commonly used nodes like Events, Debug, UdonBehaviour, as well as the Classes for other nodes like GameObjects, Ints, Networking, etc. If you pick a node from the list, it will appear. If you pick a Class, then you'll get a new search window focused on that class.
* If you want to open up the old full-search, you can do that with Tab - it will be as slow as it used to be, but should work the same.
* If you press space with an existing node selected, you will search within that node's class. So with GameObject Get Name selected, you'll see all the accessible properties and methods for GameObject when you press space. If you don't like this, you can turn it off in Settings ('Focus Search on Selected Node')
