details:
`CustomEvent` could be fired by other UdonBehaviour before `Start` is fired. So, Udon programmer who implements this CustomEvent must check already initialized or not before CustomEvent body (and do initialize if needed). It's inconvenient and waste of time (in the meaning of both run-time and writing-time of users).
I prefer to do Start before CustomEvent if it's not done yet. All of the above is same for SendCustomNetworkEvent case.
(This might be a "feature request" but I chose "bug report" section because I guess this is not intended implementation.)
SDK Version: VRCSDK3-UDON-2020.05.12.10.33

--- Details
In UdonBehaviour.cs, Udon `Start` event is fired in C# `Update` methods.
Events other than SendCustomEvent and SendCustomNetworkEvent have `if(!_hasDoneStart)` check at the beginning. So it is guaranteed that Start is fired before these events in Udon program. On the other hand, SendCustomEvent does RunProgram without `_hasDoneStart` guard.
My request is inserting same thing, that C# Update method does, into SendCustomEvent. `if(!_hasDoneStart)... RunProgram(startPoint) ...`
title: Start event should be fired before processing CustomEvent and SendCustomNetworkEvent

comments.body: This might make sense for network events since something may not have been initialized yet and it might not be in a valid state for networking. But I don't think that it should be a thing for normal CustomEvents, maybe there should be a second version of SendCustomEvent with this functionality if you want it. Because otherwise it makes it impossible to have parity with C# if SendCustomEvent is locked behind an object having already executed Start(). In C# with Unity it's totally valid to call methods on disabled objects that have not had Start called on them. There's actually a bug report for this not being the case in Udon https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/sendcustomevent-fails-on-gameobjects-that-where-instantiated-in-the-same-functio This seems like it's the intended implementation for SendCustomEvent at least, I do not know about SendCustomNetworkEvent.

details:
First: it attempts to place the nodes at the cursor. The way it does that is by picking one specific node and puts that at the cursor, then all the other nodes will be arranged around that as if they are children of it. The problem is that the node it picks is completely unpredictable. It's not random, but it appears to be the first according to some index. Because of the unpredictability, you have no idea where your nodes are going to go.

Second: once you have pasted a bunch of nodes, they are by default not selected.

These two issues combined means that it is very common to duplicate a group of nodes and they end up mashed together with a different group, so your only option is to undo and paste it somewhere else.
title: Pasting/duplicating has a couple of small QOL issues

details:
I can't speak for in-game performance, but in editor having OnGUI registered to every UdonBehaviour makes up a majority of the runtime overhead of empty behaviours. If I have 2000 UdonBehaviours in the scene with the Empty graph behaviour, it takes approximately 20ms on the CPU. Around 18.5ms of that overhead is from OnGUI. OnGUI also generates 0.7MB of garbage per frame for all of those events. Also note that OnGUI can run multiple times per behaviour.

Udon doesn't currently expose any IMGUI functions as far as I can see, so there isn't really a point in registering the OnGUI event in the first place.

---- Detail
Use case:
1. Assuming there is a node with a output port typed `string`.

I think this behaves like auto completion in text-based programming.
1. Input variable-name and separator (dot if in C#)
2. Do auto-complete operation, select a method

If the port is control flow, node's type can be used as the type for focusing.

* In the case of the node denotes an Event, then focusing to Event is useless.

details:
When dealing with custom network events, it should also include who sent the event.
So that we can check whether or not the one sent it is allowed to trigger it or not.
If it's a local custom event, sender would just be null. This would also add a layer to make sure that the custom event is only allowed locally.
Example for U#: https://gist.github.com/PhaxeNor/0a494be2d4d60f27e4f8f003321c44a2
title: Include player that sent the custom network event

comments.body: Yeah for sure NetworkEvent should always include the current owner of the object who sent the event. This I think ties pretty closely into the ability to send parameters in custom network events.

A better solution for this (and a lot of other usecases) would be to know who sent an event to be able to do this (or other checks) yourself. A public method could have a parameter of type VRCPlayerApi which is then populated by VRChat if this method is called from the network.
Should VRChat go with a different approach, please don't use a weird workaround again like an "underscore" and let us use attributes instead https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/concepts/attributes/
@{5f3287055bc2dc276e0f1630|full_name}: Being able to know who sent an event would be even better yes!

This would be HUGE, the way I was thinking was even a more naive implementation of having a method signature like "StartGame(VRCPlayerApi sender)" and VRChat filling that sender with the PlayerApi that sent it, and if the signature doesn't have a VRCPlayerApi "sender" then it doesn't do anything, like currently.

This would be HUGE for combating modded clients especially as currently the only solution to combat this is to make a synced something that then triggers the method so you can do an owner check which adds completely unnecessary complexity.

This looks to me like a low effort/high impact feature.

@{5a55f2c46765067d861f5004|full_name} My only potential thought when it comes to an implementation with an argument is it may be more confusing for Udon Graph users - do you expose an argument? Do you not? Is this the same as an existing event? Do you need to expose a new type of event?

While for U# this would be nice, and a nice way to segregate networked vs non-networked events to some degree in a less hacky fashion, I do question how confusing it may be to new and existing udon graph users with a change like this. Meanwhile a change like I initially suggested is far more backwards-compatible.
This is now available in the 3.8.1 beta SDK! Check the docs here: https://vrc-beta-docs.netlify.app/worlds/udon/networking/events#accessing-the-sender-of-an-event
@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} 84-years.gif 🙏 🙇‍♂

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} Can this sender be faked by an attacker? 

I have experienced case yesterday that one user triggered teleport for all users in the instance by sending networked events to all players. We can't even tell the name of the attacker.

I know that this could potentially be solved by adding an underscore before the name; but in some scenarios I want to compute users' interaction with local player on remote clients and communicate with local player through networked events. 

Will the attacker be able to fake the event （likely they will） and hide their names too if I implement sender check in the event handler? Is there server-side verification of the sender according to connection info?

Thank you. Looking forward to your reply!

@{5c1362e9dc3f384cc985fdb4|full_name}: While I can't give you an in-depth answer for security reasons, I can tell you that the `NetworkCalling.CallingPlayer` property is protected by VRChat's servers. That is, it is guaranteed to be accurate, even if someone uses malicious means of generating events.
@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} Thank you for your detailed reply! It is nice to hear that the information in calling player is secured. I will implement my program with this feature.
@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} Wonderful!

details:
Add ability to specify additional user defined styles (Unity style sheets) for the Graph.
Motivation:
When you fill comment node text with Japanese characters, currently it shows the text with a font for Chinese. This font is not good for Japanese users. (Maybe it is simplified Chinese font named <edit>"Microsoft YaHei"</edit>. Maybe it is used as fallbacks of default font "Fonts/Lucida Grande.ttf".) 
But if it specifies Japanese font, then it's not good for Chinese users. Most best way is handling language information with text as a rich text. But I think it's too much for this tool. Instead, if this tool has ability to specify font file, it's enough for most cases.
To achieve this, easier and generic way is specifying styles by users. So I suggest to support user defined styles.
(technically It's possible to solve it by modifying UdonGraphStyle.uss in SDK3. Of course, SDK modification is not allowed for user by TOS. Generally speaking, "technically possible things" sometimes spread out involuntarily. And it is bad educational thing for beginners, I think. So please provide us a legal way.)

comments.body:
Just by curiosity, I dug what's going on.
* Loading and pasting of previously created noodles are possible.
* Output port of `UnityEngineComponent.__GetComponent__T` is typed `UnityEngine.Object`. "Instance" port of `SendCustomNetworkEvent` is typed `VRC.Udon.Common.Interfaces.IUdonEventReceiver` So it isn't connectable. (because not assignable each other)
* If output port is typed `System.Object`, they are connectable. So new Graph Editor's type system itself seems to be fine.
* Old (current live) editor `UdonGraph.CanConnect(Slot fromSlot, Slot toSlot)` returns `true` if `(fromSlot.node.name.Contains("__T") || fromSlot.node.name.Contains("__TArray"))` . So it is connectable. (This should be at least endWith imo)
* Series of GetComponent methods seems to be the only cases that have parameterized output type with generics among defined nodes.
Added a special exception for IUdonEvent Receiver to allow its connection from any Component. We can now make this graph without jumping to 'T' overload and back:

details:
If you name your GameObject `PlayerManager`, then execution of SendCustomNetworkEvent is blocked. This behavior newly started from build 944 or 946 without any notice.

I made a world for reproduction: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_f17d2b37-2f60-47d2-b280-e4489ba29368

---
I use identical Udon program for two GameObjects. You'll see logs for the failure case (named `PlayerManager`) like this ("naqtn" is my user name):
[Network Processing] RPC called PlayerManager:UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC:All and 10 bytes
[VRC_EventDispatcherRFC] SendRPC/AlwaysUnbuffered on PlayerManager blocked for naqtn (local master owner)

---
On the other hand, the log success case (named `Foo`) is like this:
[Network Processing] RPC called Foo:UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC:All and 10 bytes
[VRC_EventDispatcherRFC] Will execute SendRPC/AlwaysUnbuffered on Foo (UnityEngine.GameObject) for naqtn: S: "UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC" I: 0 F: 0 B: Unused (local master owner)
[Network Processing] RPC invoked UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC on Foo for naqtn
[UdonSync] Foo executing echo at the behest of naqtn

---
I guess "real" PlayerManager exists somewhere (perhaps in hidden player object) and the system wants to block malicious incoming messages. It might reach with adjusted network id. But I think blocking by the name is not reliable and is not good way to do that. Because VRC_EventDispatcherRFC must be able to get the object reference of real PlayerManager internally.
I'm not sure this is a bug or intended feature. If this is a feature, please describe in the document and announce to Udon creators.
title: SendCustomNetworkEvent does not work on an object named PlayerManager

オブジェクトを PlayerManager と名付けた失敗するケースでは次のようなログが表示されます（「naqtn」は私のユーザー名です）：
[Network Processing] RPC called Foo:UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC:All and 10 bytes
[VRC_EventDispatcherRFC] Will execute SendRPC/AlwaysUnbuffered on Foo (UnityEngine.GameObject) for naqtn: S: "UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC" I: 0 F: 0 B: Unused (local master owner)
[Network Processing] RPC invoked UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC on Foo for naqtn
[UdonSync] Foo executing echo at the behest of naqtn
---
一方、`Foo`と名づけた成功するケースは次のようになります。
[Network Processing] RPC called Foo:UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC:All and 10 bytes
[VRC_EventDispatcherRFC] Will execute SendRPC/AlwaysUnbuffered on Foo (UnityEngine.GameObject) for naqtn: S: "UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC" I: 0 F: 0 B: Unused (local master owner)
[Network Processing] RPC invoked UdonSyncRunProgramAsRPC on Foo for naqtn
[UdonSync] Foo executing echo at the behest of naqtn
---
この動作は、“本物の” PlayerManager がどこかに（おそらく隠されたプレーヤー・オブジェクトの中に）存在し、システムが悪意のある着信メッセージをブロックしたいためなのだろうと想像します。Network id をうまく調節すると到達できるのかもしれません。しかし、名前によるブロックは信頼性に欠け、この遮断を行うための良い方法ではないと思います。 VRC_EventDispatcherRFCは、本物の P​​layerManager オブジェクトへの参照を内部で取得できるでしょうから。
これがバグかなのか意図された機能なのかは私には判断が付きません。もしこれが機能である場合は、ドキュメントに記載し Udon クリエイターに周知するよう、お願いします。

details:
In many graph languages these days, they include a "portal" feature to help with unwieldy, complex, and long graphs. 

With the new addition of groups, it is very useful for organizing complex graphs, however, the issue arises when you want to use outputs of these groups to other groups or sections of functionality. This would in effect create long and unsightly noodle connections which are hard to manage, harder to read, harder to understand, and more error prone because of that. If you have to ask yourself, "what is this connecting to?", because it's off of the screen, it's a bad sign.

Portals solve these issues by allowing the output of one node to effectively enter a "portal", and it can connect to the same named exit portal which then connects to a nodes input, all while hiding the noodle and at the same time telling you which portal it is, thus allowing you to know where it's coming from without following a really long noodle connection.
In my opinion, Gaea did it the best, as can be seen below.
title: Udon graph portals - For organizing complex graphs

details:
If you use a Slider and set onValueChanged to go to UdonBehaviour.SendCustomEvent, it will always send 0 even though your custom event implemented a float parameter.

The reason for this is that SendCustomEvent takes a string parameters, not a float parameter, and is therefore shown under the static section, and not under the dynamic floats section. As a result, we can't actually get the float value from the callback, leaving the Slider onValueChanged event basically useless if we want to know what value it is.

A workaround would involve passing in the Slider as a public variable, then using the callback with SendCustomEvent, and grabbing the value from the Slider component.

Not entirely sure of a good solution to the problem as SendCustomEvent would always require a string parameter so it knows where it's going. Even if custom parameters were added so you can call the function with parameters, this probably still wouldn't fix it

Not sure whether you can consider this a bug or not due to the cause, but it kinda effectively behaves like a bug
title: Unity Slider onValueChanged sends 0 float

Seems that the methods
OnBecameInvisible, OnBecameVisible
Are broken. I tested using a monoscript and they trigger properly, but they don't trigger using Udon.
Regular practices were followed in the testing, e.g.
-Object has a meshrenderer
-Has a standard shader (nothing funky)
- Scene camera is not messing with the results (closed the tab)
- No other cameras looking at it. Only camera being tested is the main camera
- Set normal callbacks as usual (using UdonSharp)
- Exact same code, except using Monoscript, works properly
- OnWillRenderObject DOES work however.

-> Using Udon 2020.06.16.20.53_Public.
title: OnBecameInvisible, OnBecameVisible, broken

comments.body:
Current workaround:
- Set a render bool to false.
- In Start(), set a global render variable. GetComponent<Renderer>();
- In OnWillRenderObject(), if render bool is false, set it to true.
- In Update(), if render bool is true, check if renderer.isVisible, if not visible, set render bool to false

I tested this in VRCSDK3 2021.06.03.14.57 and can confirm that this is still broken. 
While I was able to trigger the events in play mode (using U# and CyanEmu), they did not trigger in VRChat.

After some digging, I came to the conclusion that these events are actually available in Udon, but neither U# or Udon Graph seem to recognize them. There are also a handful of other events which aren't properly listed/recognized, and they aren't even documented anywhere. I'm not entirely sure how long these events have been around for, but they're at least available in the latest version of the SDK.

In order to use the OnBecameVisible/Invisible events right now, you can do the following:

Udon Graph:

Add a Custom Event node, and name the event _onBecameVisible or _onBecameInvisible.

UdonSharp:

Add a public void method with no parameters and call it either _onBecameVisible or _onBecameInvisible.

Bump

I believe that these methods are essential for content optimization.

As Nestorboy pointed out, we can actually utilize these events in VRChat with _onBecameVisible or _onBecameInvisible. Shouldn't they be recognized and documented so that more people can become aware of and use them in their code?
I dont want to be pushy, but is there a reason for not listing and documenting those methods? I can't believe it's that hard since those are already working in VRChat.

I've made a PR so they can be at least documented in U# docs:

https://github.com/vrchat-community/UdonSharp/pull/156

So, it would be really useful if Udon could "auto-get-component" (auto-cast) inputs if the type of Component is explicitly defined for an input. This would also be highly useful when making changes to "self" object ("self" is by default in all "instance" inputs), but since we still need to provide an exact component, we still need to add "GetComponent+Type" nodes even for "self-management". See the example image: red circles are just "self-get-component" which won't be necessary in case of auto-casting. Greens are redundant GetComponent of another variable.

Using SDK VRCSDK3-UDON-2020.07.16.10.33_Public.unitypackage it is now not possible to set object reference fields to null in the inspector. This happens on both Udon Graph programs and Udon Sharp programs. 
An easy repro is to put a public gameobject field on an Udon program and set it to reference some object in the scene. If you select the field and press delete the field will no longer get set to null whereas it did in the previous live Udon release. 
This issue traces back to a small change that happened on line 186 of UdonProgramAsset.cs where a null check was added before setting variable values that prevents you from setting null to any public variable from the inspector. This null check should be removed.
Specifically this line:
`if(!publicVariables.TrySetVariableValue(exportedSymbol, variableValue))`
was changed to:
`if(variableValue != null && !publicVariables.TrySetVariableValue(exportedSymbol, variableValue))`
and should be reverted
title: Unable to set object references to null in Udon behaviour inspector

details:
This one is hard to test, but has been seen a lot during Slaughter House development:
Storing a player's VRCPlayerApi object within a UdonBehaviour, then calling GetPosition or GetRotation shortly after the player has left the world, will throw due to a null pointer.
What's odd is that the VRCPlayerApi object is not null, and properties on the object are not set to null (such as display name). It looks like GetPosition and GetRotation are just unsafe calls during cleanup of a disconnected player.
The correct behaviour here should be to return the default values for Vector3/Quaternion if the player is in the process of being removed, rather than throwing due to a null pointer.
title: VRCPlayerApi GetPosition and GetRotation can throw due to a null ref if checked shortly after the player leaves the world.

comments.body: Our approach to this is a new static method - IsValid(object o). You can pass any object into this method and it will return True or False. For VRCPlayerApi, we're specifically checking to see if the player is still in the room. For all other objects, it will work the same as a null check for now, but can be extended in the future to check for special cases like this.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: It might make sense to make the `IsValid` method do a `UnityEngine.Object` equality when used on `UnityEngine.Object` types in addition to the `VRCPlayerApi` handling. It's not apparent in the graph what the difference is between object equality and unity engine object equality so people are liable to choose the wrong one. However, this needs to be resolved first for it to be useful: https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/null-check-on-gameobject-will-throw-exception-if-the-gameobj-is-destroyed

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: MonoBehaviour does not capture basic Unity builtin component types like MeshRenderer and such, it's only user defined types for the most part. It also doesn't capture asset types which may be destroyed at runtime such as RenderTexture.

details: After exposing Haptics without pickups (https://feedback.vrchat.com/admin/board/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/expose-vrcplayerapiplayhapticeventinhand-for-udon), it's become clear that the same settings produce different outcomes on each platform.
title: Equalize Haptics Across Platforms

comments.body:
Did some testing using a haptics test world (https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_1f9f4b44-9a69-4c99-b968-dc8555cda602) and **it would appear that the Quest is possibly mis-applying haptic values**. Unsure if this is a limitation of the Quest API, or a bug relating to the Quest client, but even with values as low as 0.05 Amplitude, and 10Hz, for a 1 second haptic event the Quest client provides a **solid buzz**, whereas on SteamVR it, *appropriately*, provides more of a "thump", similar to the haptic feedback one might find from a modern iPhone or Apple Watch.

In simpler terms, the Quest client seems unable to provide *non-vibrating* haptics at all, compared to the PC client, in such a way that suggests the "floor" for amplitude and/or frequency is *much higher* on Quest than PC.

Both tests were done on the Oculus Quest 2 too, I might note: The Quest Client is obvious, but the PC test was done via Air Link & SteamVR.

details:
Unity stores the position values of GameObjects in single-precision floating-point format. This works well for small values, which it can represent precisely; but precision decreases as values increase because of floating-point rounding errors. As a result, GameObjects rendered far from the origin (0,0,0) aren't positioned accurately (they're slightly misplaced). The effect becomes more pronounced the further the gameplay moves from the origin, and it's most noticeable during animations. So for example, instead of the player moving smoothly through the scene, their movement appears jittery.
We need a floating origin solution that shifts the world when the player is x units away from the origin. Alternatively let us do it ourselves with a "unsynced" teleport remote player. I hope you understand.
Right now world size is limited to 4-5000 units in any direction, which is too small esepcially if you are doing for example a space world, racing game, etc.
title: Floating Origin

Reality right now:
- VR player can always pick up the pickup from 20cm or so, even when the value is set way below that
- Desktop player can pick up the pickup from kilometers away, which completely breaks most map concepts, no matter what value is set
- There is no way to set this value to zero to avoid that a player can pick it up without touching the object

details:
I know this sounds dumb but please hear me out. The creation of Udon#, while absolutely incredible for programmers, has severely stinted development into the Udon graph system.
The issue is that the vast majority of people using Udon are only using U#, so a lot of the feedback and bug reports are coming from U# users. This has lead to huge flaws in the Udon graph system getting barely any attention and falling to the wayside.
As an example, Udon graphs had a bug where for no apparent reason, the graph would fail to compile. There would be no error and no way to tell it was broken until you tested it. Once you knew it was a broken, the only way to fix it was to duplicate it and delete the old one. This wasn't rare either, it happened almost every single time. This lead to many situations where you were left wondering if you made a mistake in the graph, or if it was just broken for no reason. This bug alone was directly responsible for everyone moving to U# development instead because it was so debilitating. It was reported on the canny early on but wasn't actually fixed until about 10 months later. This, in my opinion, is absolutely ridiculous. There is no way a bug that bad should have been left alive for so long. Anybody that used Udon graphs for more than 20 minutes should have run into this issue, so why wasn't it fixed earlier?
Udon# didn't have this issue, it was exclusive to graphs. I can only assume that the majority of the development team working on Udon was also using U# and didn't even know the bug existed.
The crux of the issue is that if development continues to be focused on Udon# instead of graphs, a lot of people new to world creation are going to be turned off about using Udon if basically everything is designed around U#. A lot of new creators don't have any programming experience and aren't going to learn an entire programming language just to make their own home world. The community stands to lose a lot of potential talent if graphs simply aren't being developed, tested, and bug fixed.
In essence, I'd just like more focus to put on graphs instead of U# getting all the attention. If graphs aren't maintained properly then the barrier of entry into world creation becomes monumental for newbies and will only encourage more content to be created on SDK2. Please remember that the only reason you don't see a lot of Udon graph issues on the canny is because people either get fed up and move to U# or just completely give up on trying to make it work. Making graphs more user and beginner friendly is absolutely essential if you want the community to move away from SDK2.
title: Put more focus on Udon graph development

U# is a third-party compiler plugin for unity and is not maintained by VRChat team. VRChat only officially supports the UdonGraph and the UdonAssembly langauge. U# simply compiles C# like code down into the official UdonAssembly, similar to how the graph compiles into UdonAssembly as well.
In my experience, most of the issues with Udon Graph are related directly to the graph GUI itself, rather than the raw uasm.
I will remind people that Udon is still considered alpha (as this canny name implies), so there is still much work to be done on it. Do keep in mind that the VRChat team is rather small all things considered. Patience is key.

We're constantly working on both the Udon VM and the Udon Graph to find and fix issues, as well as add new features. U# is awesome and all of its development comes from the community, not the VRChat team.

details:
One of the major hurdles with using node editors is speed of development. To work well the editor must be fast and provide ample shortcuts and other speed up tools.
UE4 blueprint / material editor are nice examples of how you can make trivial tasks like branching or variable creation much nicer.
Allowing user to hold some button alongside pressing the mouse to create a particular node like a branch or a block.
UE4 Material editor (or Unity's Amplify) also allow to create a variable in place by holding a numeric key. I think it would be pretty useful if we could do something like:
1 + left click: create bool in place
2 + left click: create float in place
3 + left click: create Vector3 in place
0 + left click: create int in place
and so on. Adding a vairable and dragging it over takes some time, so that would definitely allow for faster iteration cycle.
As a sidenote in the creation - it would be nice to be able to convert a constant into a variable with some button / right click menu. [Here's a canny for that](https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/conversion-of-constants-into-variables)
UE4 shortcut lists:
[Blueprint Editor](https://docs.unrealengine.com/en-US/Engine/Blueprints/UserGuide/CheatSheet/index.html)
[Material Editor](https://odederell3d.blog/2019/12/26/ue4-material-blueprint-shortcuts/)
title: Add node keyboard shortcuts to Udon Graph editor

details:
When i am trying use Textasset file (it's just text file) with a lot video links inside, i found out it's set as String.
I discovered and now i understand there is protection built inside Udon(Sharp) where String cannot used in videoplayer or in pictures (when VRC_Panorama alternative is ready) so i am searching for solutions.

I need find a way to make it Url variable, but Udon has nothing for String conversion. There is no String to VRCUrl, but there is VRCUrl to String conversion (kinda weird). The protection is meant to avoid changing urls in runtime (in world) and send data to servers - with IP and UserID for example. That is why String is blocked. But Url works like String... so how about this?

The VRCUrl can only added in Unity in fixed Urlinputfields but i saw you can make arrays with like VRCUrl[] or VRCUrl[][]. Arrays are allowed, but manual work to add so many urls in Unity Inspector is really frustrating work. Really waste of hours work. Why can it not bit automated?

There is with InspectorGUI conversion possible with UnityEditor, but i saw it's pretty hard and not easy to understand for people who just started to learn in Udon. Even i am more in coding, it's still hard and also it's pretty dirty way for me...

The good thing about Textasset is they are read-only, because Udon cannot change Text files. So i am thinking, why not add new function TextassetUrl to Udon? It's still safe and it's way much easier to code in Udon(Sharp) because it is directly converted in Url variable (similar like String).
Then it's easy task to split it in arrays, and then we can send it to videoplayer.
But due security part, there might some rules:
- You can use + in VRCUrl, but not with String values. It stays purely in VRCUrl. Like Filename = Serverurl + filename. Serverurl is also fixed value in Udon as VRCUrl value. Count up is not possible because Int to VRCUrl is not possible. You can still add numbers but only as fixed VRCUrl value. (But it's also possible to not allow + for VRCUrl if you dont want add too much. - means all links in Textasset must full links.)
- It's not possible change or convert dynamically in VRCUrl value, because there are no Url functions.
- The only allowed function for VRCUrl is Split function to make arrays possible (and still safe because it don't add new things)
- I guess the Split(value) may used as String or Char, because the risk is very low because it cannot add new things.
- Alternative you can add SplitUrl(value) if you want make it purely for VRCUrl, where value must in VRCUrl value. If you just make sure nothing will changed. You can set VRCUrl value like private VRCUrl splitValue = "\n" and it should stay safe.

If you add new functions like TextassetUrl, i am sure many people will happy it makes way much easier to make video listings and picture listings. With Text file, it is very easy to make listings (they can made from Excel CSV export for example) and text files are packed inside World package when uploaded to the server. There is no risk something will changed in runtime. It's all fixed anyway.
BTW it's in the end identical like VRCUrl[] or VRCUrl[][] after splitting text file. (reading with TextassetUrl.Text is directly in VRCUrl variable) So there are no differences because the outcome is same.

Without this function, it's really hard to program correctly and it's also not inside Udon possible, because Textasset output is unsafe String, and that is not possible for videoplayers and VRC_Panorama (image) loading. Please make this possible. I dont like kinda dirty work with #if !COMPILER_UDONSHARP && UNITY_EDITOR function. Make it in Udon and it's much easier and much shorter code. And it looks also more clean.
title: Make TextAssetUrl possible.

comments.body:
(... Four years later, I hit this issue)

The problematic lines are here in `UdonProgramAsset.cs`

The yellow-circled part limits the lower boundary to zero, but the red-circled part expands it to one.

Also, the `Array.Resize` method creates a new array even if the passed array was `null` and the size was zero. So you can't set (or leave) the value to `null`.

(2nd image: When the focus goes out, the size becomes `1`)

I found a workaround: Edit and keep `0` in the size field and close the fold (triangular icon before the variable name).

(It's awful but working. Actually, I think it's another bug.)

Note for the dev. The following line in the capture `if(valueArray != null && valueArray.Length > 0)` is meaningless because `valueArray` cannot be null (by calling `Resize`) and next `for` loop works well even if the length is zero.

details:
People have exploited Udon and are able to remotely call every defined function on other clients using SendCustomNetworkEvent. This gives those users a lot of power that they shouldn't have, especially since literally everything in Udon is public and has a network ID.
Easy fix: Create a tag like [Networkable] that must be defined for every function that is supposed to be triggered via network event. This would also reduce network IDs.
To further improve security, functions/methods and fields in Udon should respect the private/public declaration and should be unable to get accessed from outside this behavior when they are not declared as public. They should also have arbitrary names so that a modded client doesn't have a human-readable list of them.
title: Fix Udon Security Vulnerability (illegal network function calls via modded clients)

comments.body: non-public variables are settable via SetProgramVariable, which is similar to reflection, while there could be an option to "un-export" fields, if it defaults to making non-public fields private, it will break most existing worlds. Methods marked as private in U# will not get exported and will not be callable via name, but any built-in Unity/Udon events such as Interact are required by Udon to be public.

This was completed as of 2020.4.4.
Any custom events with an event name starting with an underscore (`_`) will be blocked from being triggered via the network. If you have custom events that start with an underscore, they will not fire via network calls anymore.
If you want to specifically prevent a method from being called over the network, use `_` as the first character of the method name. Existing Udon / VRCSDK methods are reserved, so don't use those.

There is a slight performance cost to this (plus the gotcha of not noticing it is an issue), so it is preferable for this to be fixed by the devs, but in the meantime, here is a solution I implemented.
Have the event also set a boolean to true as soon as the event was raised, and subsequent calls to the event will not perform any action if that bool is true.
Then in the Update() method, I have a timer that starts counting time since the boolean was set to true, and once that time reaches 2.5 seconds, the boolean is set back to false.
I also disable the box collider for the chair until the timer elapses, so that someone can't immediately get back into the chair before the timer has fully elapsed.

details:
I am well aware of a post that's already talking about instantiating GameObjects/Prefabs that contain UdonBehaviours, however I have dug a bit deeper to understand the cause.

Essentially what's causing the crash is the PhotonView ID being duplicated and I assume trying to replace its self.
You can notice this error if you add the Prefab to the scene and try to instantiate while using the debug logger. I attached an image showing the log error.
I noticed that you can still call methods, get variables, etc within the Prefab after you instantiate it by getting its class using the following.

'ClassName variable = (ClassName)prefabObject.GetComponent(typeof(UdonBehaviour))'

However I have noticed that some events such as Collisions (in my case) will be the death of the script whenever they occur.
A way to get around this bug (at least somewhat) is to have the prefab in the scene (nest it in an empty or something), set its active to false, then in your instantiation method for that prefab, set its active to true after you have instantiated it. You can even do it within the prefab if you call a method within it's behavior class.

Additional reference to the bug can be found here: https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/587-instantiated-prefabs-dont-have-udon-behaviours-when-in-vrc-not-editor

- SDK3 2020.11.30.20.04
- UdonSharp v0.18.8
title: PhotonView ID Duplication By Insantiation Causes UdonBehaviour's To Crash.

details:
In the graph UI, when a node has an implicit reference to the current gameObject, related transform or current script(UdonBehavior), visually indicate as such.
For example, on the UdonBehvaior -> SendCustomEvent node, the input for the udon behavior reference implicitly fills the input with the reference to the current script if the input has no connection. It should visually indicate (with text change) that the reference to be used when there is no noodle attached is the current script. 
As of now it is simply labeled "instance", which can cause confusion and make developers think that they have to explicitly provide an instance noodle connection by doing a 'Const This -> Get Component UdonBehavior' each time.
I would recommend having the text updated to something like "this script" or "current behavior" to have the visual indication that there is a value implied when no connection is present.
This visual change would be a step in the right direction for making the graphs even more beginner focused and friendly.

comments.body:
Your example would be solved by the exposure of Dictionary<T,T>.

details:
When an event has been fired, it should be possible to query the state of the event including:
- The source of the event (Local via SendCustomEvent or built-in events like Interact, Collision, etc, or Remote for network calls via SendCustomNetworkEvent)
- The object that fired the event (or null if not relevant to the event)
- The player that fired the event (LocalPlayer or null if the event source is local)
- The name of the event (should return the internal name of the event for built-in events (e.g. Interact would return "_interact", or the name of the custom event)
- Additional parameters that were passed to the event (may provide a more flexible alternative to retrieving custom event parameters)
title: Implement an event details API

details:
Here's a scenario to explain what happens:
Object has a synced int.
Player 1 takes ownership of object and sets the synced int to 5. Everybody else sees 5.
Player 2 takes ownership of object and sets the synced int to 10. Everybody sees 5 turning into 10
Player 3 takes ownership of the object without changing anything. Everybody else sees 10 turn into 5, and then a moment later it's back to 10.
This is not an issue with precise timing, as it can happen even if the object has been 10 for several minutes. Somewhere, player 3 remembers that the object used to be 5 and it is interpolating into 10 or something, even if syncmode is none.
title: When taking ownership of an object, remote players will be given outdated udon synced data

comments.body:
I also suggest to expose LightProbes and SphericalHarmonicsL2[] (SphericalHarmonicsL2 already exposed) to also allow switching of pre-baked set of lightprobes and modifying it at run-time. 
At the moment, it is very difficult to switch non-real-time lighting, for this you need to use strange methods, like copying meshes or complex non-standard shaders. And lightprobes are completely untouchable. But Unity by design has features to switch baked scene lighting. RenderSettings are already exposed, which allows creators to manage some ambient lighting settings. I see no reason not to expose access to the rest of the baked lighting settings to give creators full control over the lighting.

This would be a huge boon for a few things - but for our use, it would allow us to use bakery, and also still have RTGI that can illuminate avatars for select small areas of the world.  EDIT: I now realize that may not be as feasible as I expected.
Related: https://feedback.vrchat.com/udon/p/expose-lightmap-settings-method-to-udon

details:
I would like a way to mark stations as "local" which prevents stations from doing their own internal "seated" player tracking. This allows us to reuse 1 station for all custom world locomotion systems.
Currently stations have their own special handling for making sure that late joiners see a specific person sitting in a station that they were sitting in prior. This handling also prevents you from sitting in a station if your client thinks someone else is already in it. However, if two players enter the same station at the same time, locally they will both be registered as being in the station which means the lock out provided by VRC does not guarantee anything and is essentially useless in practice for much more than a chair that's there for aesthetics since it's trivial to break unintentionally and by extension break any systems that depend on it. Anything involving stations has historically been bug prone and liable to break subtly at the drop of a hat. When issues have been fixed, they have been liable to regress a patch or two later and then get left for months or years. The same goes for the implicit syncing behaviour of stations.
Putting aside bugs with station sync aside, even if it worked perfectly 100% of the time, there are many cases where people want to implement their own locomotion in worlds which requires absolute control over the player position and rotation locally. But at the same time does not require a "vehicle" that the player is in and directly attached to.
As far as I have heard from VRC staff, stations are the supported way to do this since we cannot control the exact position of the player, only the derivative of it (the velocity), which is janky at best, and we cannot rotate the player on any other axis than Y because the player controller is not made to work correctly with any rotation off the Y axis outside of the context of stations.
On the other side, we should also be able to locally assign a remote player to a local station. Many worlds have used this to control the local perception of the location of remote players. Allowing for non-euclidian worlds, worlds where locomotion does not behave exactly the same as VRC where people can stand on walls for instance, or more practically, large "vehicles" where everyone can be located on the vehicle which is "moving" through the world when the world is actually moving around it, but players outside the vehicle see the remote players attached to it properly.
This is all possible with how stations are currently synced, but it means that you need to have an object pool for every station in the world which is handled consistently between all clients, and it leaves stations subject to the worryingly common bugs with station sync. I have seen many people try using stations for locomotion and such only to stop because it's way more complex than it should be even though it's the way VRC tells you to do custom locomotion. There are also many worlds that you're leaving to use the jank method of pooling them which is liable to break, and on many of these worlds *has* broken when the station sync has broken. Despite it being more complex, people will make prefabs, people will make instructions for how to deal with station pooling
Because every VRC employee seems to be of the mindset of "man, should we support this basic thing that takes maybe a couple of hours to implement and should be basic to support?" I will reiterate: people already do these things, as time goes on, more people will do these things, you are increasing technical debt by *not* adding this. And it will only get worse the longer you do not act. When you run a content creation platform, lack of basic things like this pushes technical debt onto your creators, which means they use systems in ways they should not need to be used. This in turn means you need to support these further abstracted systems
Stations are the established and supported way to override VRC's built-in locomotion, and they should be able to be treated as such without hacking around to make them kinda work and leaving them subject to sync bugs.
Related bug about one of the ways station sync breaks currently:
https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/random-user-gets-stuck-in-station-for-new-joiners

details: SetProgramVariable changes the type of the variable you're setting to object, regardless of the original type or the value being passed in.
title: SetProgramVariable clobbers data types.

comments.body:
Many externs are capable of screwing with the data type on a variable, `SetProgramVariable` is one of the most easily reproducible ones though. `GetProgramVariableType` is the bigger issue, it gives you the strongbox type of a variable. Which is not guaranteed to stay the same during program execution, and it quite likely to get changed in many cases since the VM will reassign strongbox types to make things work. In many cases just copying a variable is enough to change the target variable's reported type. For `GetProgramVariableType` to work as expected in a statically typed language it should only return the original strongbox type set on a variable.
Side note: GetComponent(s)<T> apparently uses (or used, I'm not sure if it has been fixed) `GetProgramVariableType` internally which causes GetComponent(s)<T> to break when you're calling it on a variable that has been altered from its expected type of `Component` to `System.Object`.

details:
World persistency would increase usability since old in-world settings could load automatically when the user re-visits the same world later. 
As worlds get more and more complex, this is no longer a "nice to have" feature - it is now absolutely needed to make a more complex world playable (such as playing a long story through like "The Devouring" for people who don't stay 4+ hours in a single world in VR or in case VRChat crashes while playing it). 
But it is also needed for grinding mechanics and worlds where you can build something and farm resources - something we are currently working on. 
Tl;dr, either VRChat gives us a [StoreToDisk] string datatype (without a weird character limit) that saves to disk when it changes and loads again when the user joins the same world or we'll have to implement our own open-source solution reading debug log files and a third-party application running on people's PCs to send Ctrl+V to the window handle (as other world creators have already done it).
But either way, we definitely can't go on without a solution here and the current "ask a VR user to copy+paste a string" is not a good way to do it - especially since it's not crash-safe, so users lose all progress when VRChat disconnects the user randomly. But also since we still don't have a "Copy to clipboard"/"Paste from clipboard" function next to a TextInput field for whatever reason, something that would be extremely useful for VR users in general anyway.
Ideally, an instance could also specify to only load the progress from whoever created it, since it's not possible right now to know who's the instance creator in Udon, but that's only a minor follow-up issue.

I think its definitely important to be doing things like storing data on the users machine with their permission. There's the possibility of abuse if we dont. (For example, tracking users behaviors over time, and then later if any way ever becomes exposed to send the data to others, we could end up with individuals creating tracking systems that violate user rights in some manner)
One thing that comes to mind is if a company created a library they paid individuals to add to their worlds which tracked users behaviors, that not only tracked their info, but broadcasted it to all other connected users, then they had bots that roamed rooms at random, connected with other users, and collected the broadcasted data.

I wanted to do a small write-up to hopefully provide a clearer goal for this feature request, and maybe to incentivize the devs, since the earlier this is made, the earlier people can include this feature in their new projects.

VRChat already caches information, notably your user settings and the expressions menu settings for countless avatars. This feature should be relatively trivial to implement, and they would need:

1. World settings file in an existing cache location

2. Local API interface to write and delete world settings, which Udon can use

3. UI button for "Clear This World Data" on the world page view

4. "Clear This World Data" and "Clear All World Data" probably next to the cache clear section

4. Probably also a "size limit" that has a default value, but is configurable, just like the avatar download size

If they set the size limit to a default of 8 KB, you could have 131,072 world save settings files before you hit 1 GB (assuming they all max it out). 8 KB should also allow game worlds to store a significant amount of game state save information (like an insane amount). This would be enough for a pretty sizable JSON file. For example, this is 7.94 KB and ~400 lines and not even minified: https://gist.github.com/dark-swordsman/a2217935f33e49583664b2534bdf89ca#file-example-json

The feature should not be that difficult. It's just a matter of development time. I think it's a good idea to prioritize this feature so world creators can take advantage of it ASAP. It would drastically change how worlds can be used.

@{64809be191f8400f95aeb76a|full_name}: Likely gonna be 2024/5 feature together with Udon2 sadly. However if you need persistance right now, there are a few ways, including automatic ones with no user input.

Persistence is currently undergoing Closed beta testing! It's a complex system and includes some other changes to VRChat's networking system. We hope the testing goes well!

Here are some examples of how Persistence might be used:

- Saving and loading a player's progress

- Tracking their inventory or currency

- Placing items or structures in the world

- Remembering their preferences or settings

At launch, persistent data can be used in two ways:

- With "Player Objects." VRChat can automatically instantiate this object once for each player. Scripts on player objects can have persistent variables.

- With "Player Data," which is accessible from every script. It's a key-value storage system for saving and loading variables associated with a player.

If you're curious, here are a few more details on how Persistence is planned to work:

- Persistent data is stored on VRChat's servers and accessible on any of your devices.

- Udon can access the data of all players in the instance, but only while they're in the world.

The `meshInfo` exposes `mesh.vertices` and `vertices`, both are different and crucial.

details:
Currently, "Continuous" mode syncing syncs 100% of the time. However, in many cases, there are idle periods in which continuous syncing isn't needed, followed by periods in which smooth syncing is necessary.
The VRC Object Sync component does this exact behaviour, going to zero bandwidth usage when not moving, and having the ability to do this for UdonBehaviour variables would be very useful. This is particularly the case when the UdonBehaviour is attached to an Object Synced object; right now, this results in greatly increasing bandwidth usage as the Object Sync data is no longer able to go to sleep.
title: [Reliable Sync Feedback] Please add a way to sleep a continuously synced object

comments.body:
As a concrete suggested implementation:
Add a "SetSleeping" method to the Udon Behaviour. When true, the (continuously synced) component will sync only if RequestSerialization is called (in which case it syncs once, or a small number of times, an unspecified time after invocation), a player joins, or an attached Object Sync component is moving or held. When false, the component will be synced frequently and periodically.
On ownership change, SetSleeping is reset to false. User code can reset it to true in OnPreSerialization if desired.
Actually, this look a lot like dynamically switching between Manual and Continuous, so it could also be a SetSyncMode call.

Tested on SDK3 2021.02.23.11.40

details:
VRCSDK3-WORLD-2021.03.09.13.57_Public
Unity 2018.4.20f1
When many Midi Events are received, references outside the buffer range will occur.
Log
```
IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
VRC.SDKBase.Midi.VRCPortMidiInput.Update () (at Assets/VRCSDK/SDK3/Runtime/Midi/VRCPortMidi.cs:71)
VRC.SDK3.Midi.VRCMidiHandler.Update () (at <5d3e9f7f72234587a2c25e98f82b4f27>:0)
```
title: When many Midi Events are received, references outside the buffer range occur.

comments.body:
In trying to pass data into VRChat via the MIDI interface, I have also just encountered this issue.
Unity 2019.4.29f1, using World SDK 2021.08.11.15.16 and UdonSharp 0.20.2.
I seem to only be able to receive around 100-300 MIDI events before the error occurs. The rate at which the MIDI note events are sent does not seem to affect the error.
https://files.catbox.moe/r86zrx.gif
That said, I have also noticed a strange behaviour related to the error: by "warming up" the MIDI handler by sending a few short bursts of events before finally sending larger chunks, the bug can be delayed. At this point, I've seen it work from anywhere between 12,000 MIDI events to around 70,000. The error will still eventually occur.
https://files.catbox.moe/w68c6g.gif
Here's a 7z containing the project folder for my test project, as well as the HTML file for the webpage I use to send MIDI events in. Load & play SampleScene, then send in data of varying length to replicate the bug.
https://files.catbox.moe/v9y7ip.7z

I am having this problem as well.
*VRCPortMidi.cs:line 39*
```
                _data = new byte[1024];
```
Currently, the size of `_data`(byte Array) that holds the incoming data is set to 1024 bytes.
*VRCPortMidi.cs:line 61*
```
        public void Update()
        {
            if (_input == null) return;
            
            if (_input.HasData)
            {
                // Portmidi reports 4 bytes per event but the buffer has 8 bytes so we multiply count by 2
                int count = (_input.Read(_data, 0, _data.Length)) * 2;
                for (int i = 0; i < count; i+=8)
                {
                    ConvertAndSend(_data[i], _data[i + 1], _data[i + 2]);
                }
            }
        }
```
This exception occurs because the value that goes into the `count`(int) variable above exceeds the array length of `_data`.
*MidiDeviceManager:line 11*
```
        private const int DefaultBufferSize = 1024;
```
In the above section, `DefaultBufferSize` is set to 1024, which I assume is the maximum number of buffers for incoming MIDI events.
The return value of the `MidiInput.Read()` method is `Number of MIDI events copied to _data * 4`, and then doubled when calculating `count`, the maximum value of `count` is `1024 * 4 * 2 = 8192`.
In the current implementation, if more than 128 events are received in a single frame, an exception will be thrown and MIDI events beyond that will be dropped.
As a way to fix this problem...
- Change the `_data` array length from 1024 to 8192 and change the third argument of `_input.Read()` to 1024.
  Allow up to 1024 events to be received per frame.
- Change the third argument of `_input.Read()` from 1024 to 128.
  Events exceeding 128 will be processed in the next frame.
- If the value of `count` exceeds 1024, cap it to 1024.
  Process up to 128 events per frame without exception, and drop events exceeding 128.
So far this is not a big problem (because it keeps working even if an exception is thrown), but there is another problem.
If MIDI events exceeding the `DefaultBufferSize`(1024) are received, all note-offs will be triggered and subsequent MIDI events will not be received, and a crash may occur at the following times.
- (Both) Immediately
- (Client) During Scene transition (moving to another World)
- (Editor) When exit playmode
This problem can be reproduced by performing the following operations while playing a MIDI file to a Virtual MIDI IN Port created using loopMIDI, etc.
- (Both) Right-click on the window to open the context menu, and wait about 10 seconds
- (Both) Turn on the monitor (depends on the PC environment)
- (Client) Join/Leave the world
- (Editor) Focus the Editor window
- (Editor) Press Play or Pause button
- (Editor) Perform Asset import process
or...
- (Client) Load Avatar
- (Client) Open/Close in-game menu or SteamVR overlay
- (Client) Toggle Virtual Desktop Desktop/VR Mode
If you are developing a world that uses `VRCMidiListener` and are having this problem, you can make it less likely to crash in Editor by changing the `DefaultBufferSize` in MidiDeviceManager.cs to a huge value like 65536.

details:
The open beta notification post suggests that SetOwner is instantaneous, but documentation suggests a request is sent to the current owner to confirm whether the ownership transfer is to be allowed.
If an ownership transfer request is to be approved by the current owner, this implies an extra two network round-trips will be added to the time before the new owner can begin syncing values. This overhead is crucial to account for in our designs.
Please document:
1. What is the ballpark expected latency between invoking SetOwner and having new values be serialized out? Does it depend on whether an OnOwnershipRequest event is defined?
2. What happens if you set variables in the time between calling SetOwner and when the OnOwnershipRequest is responded to by the current owner? Is there a possibility that they'll be overwritten by received values in that time?
These behaviors aren't currently defined in https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/udon-networking#object-ownership and have significant implications in complex networking designs.
title: Please precisely document latency costs of ownership transfers

comments.body:
Added the information in https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/udon-networking#data-and-specs
1. Roughly the round-trip time between the executor and the owner; or if the owner did it, the owner and the receiver.
2. A race condition; you should expect that any writing done when not-owner will be overridden. Non-owners should not modify things they do not own. However, an UdonBehaviour using Manual sync should be able to do this all in one fell swoop. Using Continuous sync _may_ work in the right order but it's not always expected to do so.

details:
The new event documentation states:
> If you start your Event names with an underscore, you will not be able to call them over the network. We do this to safeguard our internal methods like _start, _update, _interact against malicious network calls. Best to avoid naming your own methods this way.
The recommendation to avoid naming our own events this way contradicts prior advice. However, it remains unclear whether we can safely use some underscore-prefixed event names without clashing with future VRChat-defined internal events. Please clarify what the recommended naming scheme is for user-defined events that should not be network invokable in this documentation.
title: Please clarify recommendations around _-prefixed event names

comments.body:
Now documented in https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/udon-networking#onownershiptransferred
The short of it is - use your own prefix that starts with an undersore for now. You can add a unique identifier like using `_u_variableName` which is not a format we will use. We decided that we will add a parameter in the event table in the future to declare events as local/remote capable instead of using this prefix workaround - we plan to increment the Udon Program version for the first time and support this new parameter for all Udon Programs identifying themselves with the new version number. This is a much larger change and will take some time before we can get it in but we feel that it's a better system design overall.

details:
https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/udon-networking#data-and-specs is really sparse. Please document the following:
- How many bytes each synced variable type takes (including variable-length arrays and strings, UTF8 or ASCII)
- How many bytes are possible to sync on a single UdonBehavior
- What happens if you exceed the limits (does the sync never happen until you change the variables to not exceed the limits? Does the whole UdonBehavior stop working? is there an error message in the console for the sender? Is there an error message for the receiver?
title: Document sync limits

comments.body:
How many bytes each synced variable type takes: It varies- it's roughly the C# data size of the variable, plus an offset of one to four bytes per variable, plus a one to four byte length if appropriate. We've added a way to see the payload size of each variable in a debug view in order for you to see the actuals for this in-client rather than trying to calculate it ahead of time (it's also subject to change so best to have access to the actual data)
How many bytes are possible to sync on a single UdonBehaviour: Roughly 200b on a continuous behaviour, and roughly 49kb for a manual sync'd behaviour. This is subject to change, these numbers have been added to the docs.
What happens if you exceed the limits: If you exceed limits it fails to raise the event and should spew errors in the logs. The UdonBehaviour should still work, the network layer isn't really aware that udon exists. The receiver has no idea that an event failed to raise. This has been added to the docs.

Events that are delayed are useful, but also tricky to use because they cannot be invalidated if the context of the delay is no longer valid (for example, a game timer that lasts ten seconds, but the game is terminated after five seconds).
The event delay function(s) should return some sort of thin object that can invalidate the delayed event or fire it immediately, or return a reference to the unique delayed event ID so that a function can accept that ID as an argument so it can be invalidated.

Thought of a workaround for how to "cancel" with CustomEventDelayedSeconds.
1. To allow only the initial call, use a boolean to block additional calls until the function is called. Reset the boolean in your target function.
2. To allow only the most recent call, use an integer to count the number of calls made. Have your target function subtract one from that integer and only run your intended code if the count is equal to one.
3. To cancel midway into any number of calls, create two integers. One to count the number of calls made. Have your target function separately subtract one from each integer if it is greater than 0. Only run your intended code if the counting integer is greater than the second integer. Upon canceling, set the second integer to be equal to whatever the current counting integer is.

After a lot of logical puzzling, I finally have a solution that doesn't rely on counting deltaTime. See the other post I made here.

title: OnOwnershipRequest return value ignored.

comments.body:
Note that there are two bugs going on here. One is unique to graphs, where it will simply not compile if the return value is set to a variable. That is still present as of UNU v5 SDK.
The second bug is that if the owner and the requester disagree about OnOwnershipRequest, the ownership of the object would get desynced and multiple people would think they have ownership at the same time. This has been fixed in build 1069, and the new behavior is this:
If the person requesting ownership returns false in OnOwnershipRequest, then it doesn't need to go further. No event will be sent and nobody else will receive the event. If they say yes, then an event will be sent and everyone receives it. But the only person where the return value matters is the current owner. If they say no, they will send an event back to the requester to make them give it back
To reduce latency and allow for setting variables immediately, the original requester will always assume that the owner doesn't disagree. So on their client, they will take ownership immediately. If the owner does disagree and they have to give it back, then the requester will see it switch back and forth and receive two OnOwnershipChanged events. In this situation, nobody else will receive the OnOwnershipChanged event because they will wait for the owner to confirm
Fixed in UnU Open Beta 1080

DESCRIPTION OF THE BUG (X):
Whenever a branched flow path is joined again, should the branch's bool have been "false", variables will be unaccessible and return NULL. Most functions, e.g. mathematical functions such as divisions, will also return NULL, even when both inputs are valid.
-----
DESCRIPTION OF THE BUG (Y):
Whenever a 2nd branch of a node references a variable that is referenced by another flow path, it will return NULL.
-----
STEPS TO REPRODUCE (how did you encounter the bug?): 
X: branch a flow path, join them back together, then return any variable. You should now have returned NULL when the lower branch path is taken. (returning a new const variable without any conversion will not cause this to happen).
Y: branch a flow path, and, in the lower path, reference (and work with) any variable node that is also referenced by the upper flow path. 
-----
IMAGES:
The Images below describe the refined code that causes these errors:
X (image with red letters):
When the boolean on the first branch (a) is true, everything works as intended. When it is false, the error occurs. 
The test outputs below, when a is false, demonstrate the following behaviour: b still prints the correct message (new const string, unchanged), c and d return NULL. iVelocity is a variable. Inserting int velocity or int number (e) from MidiNoteOn will also return NULL.
Y (Image without red letters):
Again, the branch bool being set to false and the lower path being taken, we see that the float (here 12.5) returns NULL after the toString. This does not occur if the upper debug.log is not connected to the toString node.
-----
RELATED POSTS AND BUG REPORTS:
After searching Canny and the forums, I could find the following related reports that can be related to the bugs:
1 - https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/reset-to-default-value-error (since not much information is posted here, this may be caused by the bug (X or Y) I described, especially since it appears "fairly random" to the author, just as it did to me at first.)
2 - https://ask.vrchat.com/t/why-your-time-get-time-node-is-probably-broken-and-how-to-avoid-it/2738 (While Time get Time is mentioned here, after testing, I can say that it does work, but that the error is caused by the bug I describe. You can see the author experiencing the bug Y on the lower Debug.Log node, having two Debug nodes accessing the same getTime node.)
3 - https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/erroneous-variable-behavior-with-chained-for-loops (similar issues appear on other "branching" nodes, every time the non-first pin is used)
4 - https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/subgraph-variables-cannot-be-referenced (Similar results to the bug (X or Y) in the old subgraph system. Maybe branches still use a system similar to the subgraph system, suggesting a fix by also implementing the SubProgram solution mentioned by Momo the Monster here?)
5 - https://ask.vrchat.com/t/jetdogs-tips-and-tricks/189/5 the statement "if you decide to use branches(if statements) you wont be able to link the next set of events." MAY have been incentivized by the error. Can not really be sure as not much information is given on why this statement is made.
-----
I am posting both bugs as one, as they are strikingly similar in nature and appear to be caused by the same problem. One fix here could potentially erase multiple bugs and solve multiple Canny posts, as shown above.

Currently manual sync is significantly faster than object sync and RPCs. This is fine... until you are using manual sync to replicate e.g. a control for a particle effect bound to a held object. We need a way to get these back into sync.
Some potential options include:
1. If the object sync latency is fixed, provide a way to obtain this delay so we can apply it to manually synced values.
2. Provide a way to attach synced variables that are transmitted on object synced updates, but do not prevent the object from sleeping when it's not being moved (see https://feedback.vrchat.com/udon-graph-upgrade-closed-testing/p/reliable-sync-feedback-please-add-a-way-to-sleep-a-continuously-synced-object)

comments.body:
How is this not resolved by having a manual sync object as a child of a continuous synced object? 

I've made 'proxy' objects like this before to get the best of both worlds, so to speak, and I've not had any issues. Since a continuous sync script still runs locally with immediate results, this proxy script doesn't provide any noticeable drawback when forwarding any events. For instance, using 'Interact()' in your continuous script and calling a custom function in a manual script with 'yourManualScript.SendCustomEvent(_proxyInteract)' and the manual script having 'public void _proxyInteract()'. This '_proxyInteract()' function can then in turn do any manual sync function you need while also keeping the continuous sync functionality of whatever your host object is. You can already have the best of both types of sync by doing this and you can see it in the AnthroNorthwest VR world with the food items I have there.

@{5f7d549362370d3eddd862f7|full_name}: the main issues with that approach are 1) complexity 2) the risk of ownership getting out of sync between those two objects and 3) additional bandwidth usage due to the overhead of having an additional object (this can to either way depending on the circumstances)

You’re right it can be worked around but it would be nice to avoid the complexities that workaround introduces.
@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: Very well put and thank you! Absolutely would love to simplify things and optimize!

details:
When there is heavy transmit activity on a single frame, manually synced events can be dropped without retransmitting.
I've been unable to create a _minimal_ repro thus far, but I do have a consistent repro world for you at least: wrld_ca2bb56a-19c1-4ef5-8ef6-d060ae9fd8b0
Repro steps:
1. Connect two clients. In each, click the big vase next to the pens to enable world debugging options.
2. Click the shuffle button on either client and wait for shuffle to finish
3. Now, click the 'tile state histograms' button on the debug panel on both. The 'synced' values that appear should be the same (but, due to this bug, sometimes aren't). These directly measure the number of manually synced objects with a particular value for a synced state variable.
4. Click 'reveal tiles' on non-master to trigger another flurry of activity, then perform the histograms check on both again. The correct behaviour is for all of the synced variables to go to state 5, but in fact, on the master only about 100 change to 5, and the rest remain as they were.
Video of repro procedure: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fy3SG2qRTzo
This does not repro every time, but it seems to happen more than half the time for me. When it occurs, it seems that often, exactly 100 manually-synced objects are transmitted (and the rest remain unsynced until the next RequestSerialization), suggesting there might be an undocumented limit of some sort here.
If you're examining this in the editor, the objects in question are named "ManualSync" and each have a single synced int.
title: Manual syncs can be dropped during heavy network load

details:
It would be useful to be able to direct a VRCPlayerAPI to copy its voice locally to one or more specified audio sources. This would disable the network voice distance checks for the duration that the player api is directed at an audio source and force them to always send voice.
As https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/working-microphone-script has been closed I'm making a new canny in the Udon board since Phase said I should and I can't find a relevant one.
The player api voice settings are useful for many circumstances, but they lack control for if we want to relocate players voices. For instance if I wanted to make a walkie talkie, or an intercom system in a world, I'd need to settle for a unspatialized "voice of god." Even for stage performances where I want the voice to come from speakers in the world, it removes from the immersion to the point that I wouldn't really want to use the voice settings API.
A plus would be if this was implemented in a way that we could put stuff like high pass filters on the audio source and have them affect the voice that's mirrored to the audio source. This may involve a VRC-specific component to use as the target which goes on the same game object as the audio source.
It would also be nice to be able to send multiple player's voices to a single output. But not absolutely necessary since we could handle it if need be by having a different source for each player. If it were included, it'd be good to be able to control the volume of each player's input to the source.
title: Provide API to copy a player's voice to specified audio sources

details:
Since VRChat doesn't want modded clients but seems to do absolutely nothing to detect them and ban those users, we've seen a flood of Udon-related malicious mods recently which can mess around with the overall experience that map creators have been added through Udon. 
We can't expect every map creator to fully seal their creations against those clients, especially since the current system lacks any authentication of where a network event is coming from, making it way too easy for modded clients to abuse that system and most times impossible to secure the world against them. 
However, I've found out that it's extremely easy to detect some of those mods, and really don't understand why VRChat isn't doing the same. Do you want people to run around in worlds and ruin the fun for everyone? Have you ever tried staying in a public lobby without getting crashed by the same 5 people that do it every day?
Tl;dr, I'm willing to do it for you, please give me an API that I can use to self-report those users when my worlds detect one of their malicious mods. It's trivial to detect and even more easy to put booby traps everywhere which those hack0rs will fall into. 
Additionally, a world should also be able to self-disconnect a client on demand. And we need network events that pass a parameter of the player that sent the event, authenticated from the PUN server, not the sender itself. Ideally, we would also get an API that would allow us to use private/public keys to authenticate that a synced string has been set by the user that has the corresponding private key.
I'm aware that this is a neverending story and that there will be mods that can bypass this sooner or later, but we creators/users really just want to see that VRChat is doing at least some minimal effort against those malicious clients and are not letting them all get away with it. If there is some kind of fear that you actually ban users who run around messing with other people through malicious mods, they will reduce in numbers. It's usually not the "new user" that uses malicious mods, it's the "trusted user", which shows that there is nothing happening to ban them. Users speak openly about their mods and about crashing others in public lobbies as if they have absolutely nothing to fear, which unfortunately also seems to be the case as of now. I really hope this changes.
title: Add Self-Report API to Udon

comments.body: And what prevents a bad actor from abusing said API? this quite the double edged sword which can do way more harm then it can do good

You just need to randomize it to be undetectable, it needs to look like part of the world / normal client behaviour. This can easily be done with Udon itself btw., we do it already in our world, we just can't do anything meaningful based on that information as of now.

In the following program, I do some math to produce a "true" value which I assign to a variable. details:
There is a claim in the documentation that "Manual synchronization is intended for data that changes infrequently and where intermediary values matter; like the positions of pieces on a chess board."
However, if you try sending a new value (and calling RequestSerialization() ) each frame, you'll find that data is skipped - not every frame gets a serialization event. Docs should call out that RequestSerialization will cause variables to be captured at some point in the future, not necessarily on the same frame.
title: Clarify that manual synced variables are not captured immediately on RequestSerialization

To elaborate, all that's strictly necessary is an *active* GameObject with an Audio Listener -- its scale will get set to 1/trackingScale, for mysterious reasons. Adding the Audio Distortion Filter, which depends on the Audio Listener, prevents it from getting deleted. It does cause an error to be emitted in the console every time you enter playmode, though. details:
It would be great if MIDI Note On messages with a velocity of 0 never made it to the On MIDI Note On node, and were rerouted to MIDI Note Off instead. 
The MIDI spec states "A receiver must be capable of recognizing either method of turning off a note, and should treat them identically.", which can be implemented using nodes, but is a hassle that can cause bugs due to combined flow paths(img 1, ignore the iNumber and iVelocity, they are integers I needed for my program), and is not considered by anyone. I have not seen a single map following this specification yet, proving to me that simplifying the process by automatically rerouting to Midi Note Off would be useful.
The MIDI spec mentioned can be found at https://www.midi.org/specifications/midi1-specifications/m1-v4-2-1-midi-1-0-detailed-specification-96-1-4 on page 10 with the title "NOTE-OFF". A screenshot of the relevant part is attached(img 2).
title: Reroute MIDI Note On with velocity 0 to Note Off by default
