details:
Currently, the behavior when the bandwidth limit is exceeded seems to be that a single UdonBehaviour can queue up an arbitrary amount of data in the transmit queue. This can take tens of seconds to flush out, in some cases. This does not seem ideal; there's not a good way to detect when this is happening and back off to reduce bandwidth usage, so this could easily result in death runs where things get further and further behind.
I would suggest that, if a single UdonBehaviour has too many untransmitted serializations, then any RequestSerialization calls be deferred until the queue can be flushed.
You can reproduce the problem behaviour in this world: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_cea2ef6d-13b3-439a-b876-539bb1691f57
Enter 4096 in one of the text boxes to start (attempted) transmitting way faster than the bandwidth limit. Let this run for a while, then set it back to 1. You'll see that (on the receive side) the received sequence numbers are well behind _instancewide_ for quite some time.
title: [Network Beta] Don't allow a single manually synced object to queue an arbitrary amount of untransmitted data

comments.body:
To expand on this a bit after seeing some confusion in discussions on discord about why this is needed - this fundamentally boils down to needing a way to help different UdonBehaviours and GameObjects to cooperate and share the limited bandwidth available in a fair manner.
In another Canny, there was a note that a getIsClogged will be added. This helps a bit, but it doesn't quite help enough. Consider if we have two UdonBehaviours that both want to send data. UdonBehaviour A checks getIsClogged, sees that it returns false, and proceeds to transmit. The network becomes clogged, and UdonBehaviour B sees that and refrains from transmitting. Later, the clog clears, but again UdonBehaviour A checks first, and transmits again (perhaps its timer for checking is shorter than B?). B never gets a chance to transmit. This is further complicated if there are multiple UBs on the same GameObject as well. This kind of pathological behavior can only be avoided with some kind of central control of when different GameObjects get a chance to transmit.
Explicitly setting a throttle in user code doesn't help either, because the network bandwidth cap is subject to change, the amount of bandwidth used by a sync operation is nontrivial to compute, and because if we set a throttle in a prefab for distribution, the value that throttle should have depends on what else is in the world and what it's doing at the time.
Finally, many prefab authors aren't going to be experts in network congestion control, and if you ask them to implement congestion control algorithms, they will get it wrong, guaranteed (but it'll probably work okay when they're testing in isolation!).
My proposal here is for a minimal change to help ensure that 1) UdonBehaviours share bandwidth in a fair manner, 2) latency doesn't get out of hand and 3) in most cases, prefab authors don't need to think about congestion control. This doesn't change existing semantics, because already RequestSerialization doesn't _immediately_ serialize, but waits a bit.
Simply making sure that Udon always waits for the queued data from a particular GameObject to finish sending before queueing up more ensures a more-or-less round-robin allocation of transmit opportunities among all GameObjects, limits the peak latency of transmission, and is probably what you want anyway for what is probably the majority of use cases where the final state of the synced vars is all that matters.
Fixed in UnU Open Beta - build 1091. Reliable sync is now rate limited as a factor of the data size. The more you send, the more your rate is limited.

details:
Some manually synced objects are more critical to sync quickly than others - you might have some that need to sync a large amount of data (which might tie up a significant portion of the transmitter's bandwidth) but can do so slowly while others you'd like to respond immediately.
Currently, the bandwidth limit for manually synced objects seems to be instancewide, so if there's a single bandwidth hog it'll penalize everything. Having a way to set a QoS or priority value on a gameobject would allow the world author to select what suffers and degrade gracefully when bandwidth limits are exceeded; it would also greatly simplify bulk transmissions.
title: [Network Beta] Allow specifying QoS/priority of manually synced objects

details:
Found on World SDK3 2021.03.22.18.27
When using OnEnter/ExitTrigger, you can collide with the chair on an avatar and reference its gameobject. Even though this gameobject is protected and not valid it will still pass Is Valid & Null checks. Once you try to use this gameobject for anything it will crash the behavior.
The attached image is a simple graph that can be used to test this, just throw it on an object with an IsTrigger collider and run into it with an avatar chair. You'll see in the log that it will print the name of the collider and then the behavior will crash.
title: Avatar chair gameobjects pass Is Valid & Null checks but are not valid

comments.body:
Update: further testing has revealed the actual issues. First, its not just avatar chairs that pass Is Valid but also the player's handheld camera (and probably some other things I didn't bother to test). Is Valid itself seems to be bugged when testing protected objects.
Second, protected objects CAN be tested Null successfully using Equality or Inequality, but NOT Equals. This isn't necessarily problematic by itself, except that when using Noodle Search with Collider Other it won't show Equality or Inequality, only Equals. This is what lead me to believe that avatar chairs passed null checks.
In conclusion, this was a perfect storm of stupidity that culminated in me losing 3-4 hours of my life.
We'll fix this by checking whether an object is protected when it triggers a collision, and the event will be dropped if it is.

We've merged in a fix for all Trigger and Collision events, which will prevent them from firing on UdonBehaviours when colliding with protected objects.
There is another issue with IsValid, which is returning True for protected objects. We'll fix this separately.

Specifically, I would like a clear point when I can know, for sure, that:
1. We know whether we are the instance master or not
2. RequestOwnership is expected to work normally

details:
ORIGINAL BUG

Steps To Observe Behaviour:
1. Create two objects with VRC_ObjectSync components.
2. Add a VRC_Pickup script to one of the objects. 
3. Use the new networking debug menu that shows ownership, priority and data transfer per second to check the priority state of the two scripts.
Steps to Reproduce Bug:
1. Create an object with an ObjectSync script.
Expected Outcome:
You should be able to just mark an object sync object as Important without having to attach a dummy pickup script (and the associated dummy rigidbody)
Actual Outcome:
You're forced to add a pickup script to mark a sync object as high priority.

===

After Vowgan and I did more testing, we're getting less consistent results. I don't understand the logic for how something is Important - it seems like attaching a pickup script might help? Maybe if the syncer is enabled whilst it's in the player's view?

It'd be good to get some information on how Important/Normal priorities work and if the above (attaching a pickup script) actually makes a synced object higher priority as this is quite confusing at the moment.

===

Some more testing - it seems like ObjectSync is very inconsistent. Attaching a pickup has had the effect of actually totally desyncing the pos/rot of the ObjectSync'ed object in testing after doing a FlagDiscontinuity on the ObjectSync.

We're also seeing five-second lag on ObjectSync'ed objects in certain circumstances, generally again after firing FlagDiscontinuity on the ObjectSync.

(Apologies for this odd bug report - this is what happens when weird behaviour is observed *after* observing something in engine...)

===

We're using my pool test world to explore this behaviour: https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_7c23c9c3-fa6f-40ed-8f75-776fed2eef4e - I'll add some instructions for how to use the synced pickup system for QA to take a look at if they're interested.

@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: What do you think about this phrasing instead:
This node is used in Manual Sync mode to flag the variables on the target UdonBehaviour for Serialization during the next Network Tick, which does not happen every frame. Example: you have a synced float variable called 'sliderValue'. When a UISlider's value changes, you trigger RequestSerialization, which triggers an OnPreSerialization event during the next Network Tick. When this event triggers, you set 'sliderValue' from the current value of the slider, and everyone in the instance will receive this new value.

details:
Use the following world to test. I advise using three clients, ideally with three remote players, and use the two non-instance owners to do the test.
https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_7c23c9c3-fa6f-40ed-8f75-776fed2eef4e
To reproduce:
1. Find the two buttons in the world that spawn pickups: a sword or a gun. You can use these to spawn up to about 100 pickups.
2. As a remote player, not the instance owner, spawn a pickup. Pick it up and hold it.
3. Have another non-owner take the pickup out of your hand.
Expected Behaviour:
The underlying VRCObjectSync should sync about as well when commanded by the new owner. 
Actual Behaviour:
The ObjectSync is heavily lagged. The effect is that the pickup looks like it's flying behind the player like a drone, rather than being held in their hand.
Additional Notes:
This appears to not occur if you drop the pickup, and then your friend picks it up from the floor.
title: VRCObjectSync'ed objects can become lagged when transferred

comments.body:
Technical notes: What I'm doing is that there's an owned VRCObjectSync that is *not* on the pickup object, but instead on a child object. When you hold the pickup, you own the sync object, but for everyone else you tell the child object sync to be the parent of a clone of the pickup. Holding the pickup inverts the syncer-pickup relationship for everyone.
I'm unsure why this is happening, but this level of bad sync is unusually bad by VRC standards.
This is still a notable issue: see You Are the Detectives #1 for magical floating objects that float behind their holder for up to 5 seconds. :(

There's two issues here:
First is that a VRCObjectSync that is not held will have *slightly* more latency than when it is held. At the moment, this is an intentional limitation of object sync. If that is ever improved, that will be classified as a feature request not a bug fix. It should also probably have it's own separate canny.
The second issue here is that object sync used to have *significantly* more latency for a moment after transferring ownership. This issue was fixed in 2022.1.1. For that reason I am marking this as complete.
https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrchat-202211
-Udon synced objects are now less likely to rubber-band when transferring ownership

details:
Issue:
When designing multiple worlds meant for navigation, IE an exploration based network of worlds that encourages groups of players to 'roam' between worlds, naturally exploring, it is currently extremely unreliable to expect players who all go through the same portal to actually end up in the same instance on the other end.
To compensate for this, world designers often opt to build larger monolithic worlds. This has negative consequences for the servers and players. If a player were to visit a world and only explore one quarter of it, they had to load and store 75% of the world unnecessarily, and the server had to consume those resources and bandwidth as well.
Proposal:
Some form of options on the portal object to be a new instance when spawned, inheriting the same privacy settings as the instance the portal was spawned in.
Effectively, when this is specified, upon the new instance containing the portals is generated, each of the portals also bind to a new instance. However, that of course would likely have disastrous effects, since you can create an infinite loop by just linking two worlds in a feedback loop together.
To solve this, two things probably are best to handle this.
1. The portal will lazy bind, only actually generating its instance the first time a user enters it
2. Portals should have some logic to detect if the world id they point to is the same as the world Id they were generated from. So if World A has a portal to World B, and World B has a portal to A, if I Go from A to B via instance generation, the B>A portal should use the instance it "came from" rather than generating a new one.
The intended effect here would be such that if a user hops through a portal to a new instance, then returns back via a "return" portal that world happens to have setup, they can semi reliably expect to end up back in the instance they came from with their friends again.
(Caveats of course for if this would involve them trying to join an already full instance, in which case it would overflow them to a new instance as a fallthrough)

If there is an intention specifically to encourage meeting of strangers behind the current design, then there is potentially one more caveat to add to the portal's instance selection, and that would be a "Fit First" sorting to instance selection.

This would effectively prioritize, rather than spinning up a new instance, instead selecting a "everyone can fit" instance if possible. For example, if World A has 8 users in it and a portal to World B, which has a max capacity of 24 users, the portal would first attempt to find a currently existing instance that *also* has room for all 8 users to fit into, and prioritize that zone first.

Reason:
A fair number of world builders, myself included, are really seeming to dig more into the artistic and design style of building individual worlds that cohesively "glue" together to encourage and reward players for taking portals and exploring, which I believe is a core design philosophy of the VRC team.
However, player's suspension of disbelief and engagement becomes interrupted often when they attempt to travel between worlds and often find their group of friends becomes broken up and scattered across different instances.
This "downside" encourages world designers to instead opt into more monolithic, larger style worlds that manually handle exploration/trave/teleportation within the world itself.
Unfortunately, these large monolithic worlds are quite the burden, if not incompatible, with quest users, which appears to be an important demographic for the VRC team.
In order to encourage world designers to "break up" their worlds into managable sizes (which lowers hardware requirements and encourages lazy loading of unused assets not explored), it is imperative a more cohesive logic be baked into how portals between worlds works.
Summary
If we make portals less random feeling and more consistent between worlds, it will encourage world makers to make more smaller worlds, rather than unified monolithic worlds, which is better for Quest users for sure, and probably just better for server health/bandwidth overall.
title: Add support for "New Instance" synched to first enter on Portals

details:
One serious issue with main-thread heavy processes is that heavy mathematical calculations sitting on that thread can seriously slow down the runtime.
Udon especially has this problem due to the high CPU load of even individual mathematical operations compared to native Unity C#.
A proposal to help with this would be to draw on the Node developers' solution to this same problem. Node, like normal JS, is based on a single thread that is designed to interact with the DOM. However, the Node developers recognized that a worker thread system would allow them to pull heavy mathematics jobs onto different threads.
This model seems like it would be interesting to explore with Udon. Some reading is below:
https://nodejs.org/api/worker_threads.html
https://livecodestream.dev/post/how-to-work-with-worker-threads-in-nodejs/
https://nodesource.com/blog/worker-threads-nodejs/
title: Add Node.js style "Worker Threads" to offload CPU-heavy mathematics etc. to

details:
# Problem
If an Animator and an UdonBehaviour are components of the same GameObject, the Root Motion setting in the animator is disabled.
# Why it's a problem
Root Motion is normally **enabled** by default on Animators. Adding an UdonBehaviour can unexpectedly break animators.
# Workarounds
- Don't put Animators and UdonBehaviours onto the same object if you want to use root motion. (However, this prevents us from using Animation Events!)
- Use the following U# code proposed by CyanLaser
```
OnAnimatorMove() {
     animator.ApplyDefaultRootMotion();
}
```
# Proposed fix
Add a toggle to UdonBehaviours which lets us directly control the root motion setting.
# Related
https://ask.vrchat.com/t/fix-for-animator-apply-root-motion-position-and-rotation/296
title: UdonBehaviours disable Root Motion on Animators

details:
When a player leaves the instance or enters a station, OnPlayerTriggerExit does not fire for any trigger colliders that they were in. 
This will break any system trying to count the players in an area.
It is known that Unity will not fire OnTriggerExit when either deleting the collider or disabling colliders, but you must move the collider out of the area. 
Example world:
wrld_d3e81903-54d6-4562-a968-2223c368906e
World has a blue trigger area and will display when a player enters or exits. There is also a chair in the area. 
Test case 1:
- Have two or more players in the room. 
- Have one player enter the area 
- Have that player leave the instance. 
- Note that a player exit trigger message is never displayed.
- Expected result would be that OnPlayerTriggerExit fires, which would then display the message
Test case 2:
- Have one player enter the blue area.
- Have that player sit in the chair.
- Notice that player exit area does not fire. 
- Have the player exit the chair.
- Notice that player enter does fire and the count is now off by one. 
- Expected result would be that on entering a station (which disables the player collider), Player trigger exit fires.
title: [1097] OnPlayerTriggerExit does not fire on player leave the instance or enter stations

details:
When reading a variable in Udon, the visible execution flow does not pass through the node. All that is known is that the read occurs some time before its value is used.
However, when the variable in question is set earlier in the execution flow[within the same event], it is not clear from the graph whether or not the read occurs before or after the set.
However, it gets even worse when the output of the same variable read node is used both before and after the set in the graph[on the same event execution flow].
Is the read performed again after the set(effectively splitting a variable read node into two nodes), or is the output from before the set held on the stack?

My proposed solution is adding a variable get node that does pass through the visible execution flow, to specifically define when the read occurs(the existing variable get nodes' behaviour wouldn't be changed)

See the attached images for example graph snippets where the order of reads can change results but isn't apparent from the graph.
title: Order of variable reads unclear.

At the moment, making a player locally disappear from view for you requires messing with VRC Stations in a way that they were not really intended to be messed with.
There's a few good reasons why a Udon toggle for being able to make a player totally disappear would be a good idea:
1. In game worlds, allow for 1 player sections, like cutscenes or tutorials.
2. In private events, allow for vetting of a guest before they show up to anyone outside of a whitelist.
3. In large maps, allow for area load/unload within the high-precision space near origin without seeing another player walking around on a different bit of the map.
4. Performance - allowing a large number of people in a map but allowing players to limit the load somewhat if they have a weaker PC.
Note that much of this is already possible with hacky implementations using stations. A visibility toggle just makes this easier.
title: Add a hide/show toggle into VRCPlayerApi

MonoBehaviour.OnRenderObject() gets called on every frame on every script in the scene that has it declared.
UdonBehaviour having every Unity event declared causes OnRenderObject() to be called on every UdonBehaviour in the world even if they don't have anything in them, which can quickly add up to a significant increase in frametime.
With 10000 empty UdonBehaviours in the scene I ended up with the following results:
	1) Unity Editor: ≈4.2ms (≈240 FPS)
	2) VRChat: ≈14.7ms (≈70 FPS)
Here are 2 more worlds in VRChat as a point of reference:
	1) Empty plane: ≈2.4ms (≈410 FPS)
	2) 1000 empty UdonBehaviours: ≈5.2ms (≈190 FPS)
I have attached an image of the Unity Editor deep profiler timeline showing that OnRenderObject() gets called on the UdonBehaviours at the end of the frame
Also in case of any misunderstanding about the meaning of "OnRenderObject" I want to state that it has nothing to do with having a renderer component attached to the same object - "OnRenderObject is called after camera has rendered the Scene"
Unity also clearly states the following in their documentation: "Be aware that this function can have a performance impact because it runs on for every GameObject with a script that uses this callback."
https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnRenderObject.html
title: UdonBehaviour.OnRenderObject() causes inevitable unnecessary static overhead

details:
While attempting to build a multiplayer arcade cabinet, I ran into a somewhat unintuitive behaviour. 
Setting Ownership to another player in the same tick as updating a synced variable and requesting serialization causes a race. Sometimes the targeted player receives ownership *before* the latest synced variables. Other times they receive it *after* the latest Synced variables. This means that logic can be unpredictable / inconsistent, as the normally garaunteed manual sync becomes, well, less garaunteed. 
I am not sure if it is the intended behaviour, but if it is it should probably be spelled out in the docs at least (responding to or closing this would serve as documentation too! :) )
In the end I was able to work around the race condition by sending a playerId along with the rest of the synced data and using that in the OnDeserialized hook to set ownership with a garauntee of having the latest data, but this seems convoluted and unintuitive, so I'd prefer to see it patched so other folks don't spend a few hours pulling hair out.
Either way, thanks for your time! <3
title: Setting Ownership to someone else in the same tick as RequestSerialization causes a race condition

details:
Right now we can only do `SendCustomEvent` via an animation file while the animator is on the same gameObject as a UdonBehaviour. There are various ways to do this within a state, but it will still require a animation file.
However, if we had a StateMachineBehaviour for SendCustomEvent (and Set Variable) we could do this without needing extra animators, and potentially not have the requirement of needing a UdonBehaviour on the same gameObject as the animator. Possibly reducing the overall UdonBehaviours in a scene depending on the creators need.
Whether or not it will support all the state machine behaviour methods will be a design/performance choice.
https://docs.unity3d.com/540/Documentation/ScriptReference/StateMachineBehaviour.html
SendCustomEvent
- State Method (OnStateEnter/OnStateExit/OnStateIK/OnStateMove)
- UdonBehaviour
- value
Set Variable
- State Method (OnStateEnter/OnStateExit/OnStateIK/OnStateMove)
- UdonBehaviour
- name
- value
Alternative
- State Method (OnStateEnter/OnStateExit/OnStateIK/OnStateMove)
- UdonBehaviour
- Type (Send Event / Set Variable)
- Name? (Set Variable)
- Value
These are just examples, and will not reflect on how or if VRC will implement it.
title: SendCustomEvent/Set Variable StateMachineBehaviour for animators

details:
When using the OnVariableChange call back for variables, synced variable changes and SetProgramVariable() both will update the variable and call the callback. These methods will also update the old value saved, but only before calling the callback and not after. The old value is left in a bad state. This means that a combination of SetProgramVariable/OnDeserialization followed with changing the value directly in Graph (or CyanTriggers) will not have the proper old value during the change callback.
Note, this affects both UdonGraph and CyanTriggers.
VRChat build 1114
VRCSDK3 2021.07.13.13.39
See screenshot for example graph. The graph contains an interact to change the variable directly, a "Toggle" event to change the variable using SetProgramVariable, and an OnVariableChange event to react to either. If you call the "Toggle" event and then call the "Interact" event, the OnVariableChange event will have both value and oldValue equal to the same data.
title: OnVariableChange old value not updated with SetProgramVariable or synced variable changes

comments.body:
After discussing with Merlin, it is suggested that the compilers should be handling setting of the old value at the end of the change callback. This means that this canny is more a bug for the UdonGraph compiler and not the runtime handling of when the change callback is called from SetHeapVariable.
From my point of view, it is still unclear on vrchat's intentions if runtime should handle this or the compiler. It would be nice if there was better documentation on handling these events for compiler writers. Since writing this canny I have updated CyanTriggers to set the value at the end of the change callback.
Closing after conversation with CyanLaser on how this is handled in the GraphCompiler.

details:
By default, a user can always grab a pickup with the other hand while holding it with one hand, to switch hands. 
This becomes a problem e.g. when you create a controller that needs to be held in one hand and operated with the other hand, sudden unwanted hand switches can occur, you cannot make the user press "grab" with the other hand in reach of that pickup. This also becomes a problem e.g. if you want to track something while the pickup is held, because the OnDrop+OnPickup event will fire while still holding it, even though it was never dropped.
We need the ability to disable hand switching on a pickup without dropping the pickup first. 
Unfortunately, disabling the "pickupable" property in OnPickup does not already enable this behavior. I would at least expect that doing that leads to the wanted result of disallowing a hand switch.
title: Disallowing Pickup Hand Switch

details:
It was only a matter of time until an exploit would break every Udon-based user authentication system over night, but here we are.
Affected is:
- every Udon moderation tool
- every Udon whitelisting tool
- every Patreon enhancement system
- every access control system for private worlds that should stay private until they are released, but need to have public test user sessions
The situation right now: People go in worlds, gain access that they should not have, and ruin other people's fun by pretending to be the world author.
Here is my proposed solution which would allow us to "fix" this:
1. Private user certificates
- every user needs a private certificate in their client, which can be used to encrypt or sign a synced string in a function like EncryptString(string input) which returns the string encrypted with that local private certificate.
2. Public user certificates
- every user needs access to the public certificates of other users to be able to decript a string in a function like DecryptString(string encryptedStr, string userID)
- the userID needs to be the one from the VRChat website, or alternatively the display name (please don't), only having the public certificate from others in your current instance would not be enough
The goal of this is to allow a safe user-to-user communication in which you can trust that whatever arrives on your side from the network to really be from that specific user, and that a user who pretends to be user X is able to decrypt a secret string which was encrypted by that user's certificate once. On top of that, authenticating a network-event (knowing where it came from) would also allow additional security.
title: We need User Certificates ASAP

comments.body: Note: I already reported the exploit in a ticket, but will not describe it here, since I don't want to draw attention towards this and risk that even more people use it.

I'd like to propose some hardening on this issue.
Private keys would be used to sign messages/strings to be sent to other users. A function would be named like SignMessage(string input). It would create a concatenated string of at least world id, world version, world asset hash, unique instance id, user id, current datetime, a nonce and the input, then hash (actually, HMAC input with the extra data as key) and sign this with the private key and return an opaque string containing the signature, user id, current datetime and nonce that can be sent over the network.
Public keys would be used to verify message/strings with a function like VerifyMessage(string input, string signature), it would extract signature, user id, current datetime and nonce from the signature, do some sanity checks, like the user id even existing in the session, the current datetime being close to actual current datetime and the nonce not having been used by the user id yet. If those checks are good, recreate the concatenated string from the SignMessage call, creating the hash and compare it to the decrypted hash from the signature. If they are the same, return the user id, else return null or error.
Also an important information that needs to be added to the documentation is, to never use SignMessage on strings sent by others over the network. Always generate the input at the client.
To improve authenticity inside VRChat network stack, I'd suggest to generate a DH-key pair during login and sending the public key part to login servers. When a client connects to an instance, it'd receive the instance's public key. Then they use DH key agreement to create a shared secret, which they can modify (like PBKDF) to use as key to sign network packets. This key pair cannot be used securely with the SignMessage method above though.

Nothing worse when you upload a world as private to do some testing and client users save the world to access when ever they want without your permission, then pose as your username in order to use whitelist settings or as you mentioned pose as the creator.

details:
Create a way to make Udon Behaviours executed server-side (by putting the server as the default owner of objects for instance).
This would allow more stability for multiplayer games. It could reduce by twice the latency and solve the problems when the master goes afk or crashes.

details:
When using sendChange on a synced variable, the owner and remote clients will have inconsistent results when the variables remains the same:
The owner will activate the Change event for that variable every time regardless if the variable was actually changed, whereas remote clients will only activate the Change event if the variable has actually changed.
Attached is a picture of an example graph for testing the problem, where every 2 seconds the SyncedInt is changed to the number 7. The results will be that the owner will print 7 to the log every 2 seconds, but remote clients will only print it once (because the value is changed from 0 to 7 initially)
title: [SDK 2021.07.13.13.39] Variable Change event inconsistent between owner and remote when the variable is not actually changed

1069:            foreach ((string symbolName, object _) in programVariables)
1070:            {
1071:                if (!_symbolNameCache.TryGetValue((eventName, symbolName), out string newSymbolName))
1072:                {

details:
VRChat introduced graphics settings in the beta client now, which modifies the LOD bias, resulting in LOD0 not being active when it should.
This is breaking some scripts in our world, because the Update() loop checks for LOD0 being rendered to know that the player is close and the object is in sight before running code.
Toggling script logic via LOD renderer (specifically LOD0) is a common way how optimization in UDON is done right now, which is also from the official Unity tutorial https://learn.unity.com/tutorial/fixing-performance-problems
VRChat cannot argue that we should use area toggles everywhere instead, since those still have their own issues which makes them unusable in some cases https://vrchat.canny.io/bug-reports/p/colliders-that-are-not-on-the-mirrorreflection-layer-will-stop-the-hand-raycasts
To solve this, we should be able to define our own graphics settings overrides, which would solve the LOD bias issue that we now need to account for. At least the LOD bias should be optionally defineable for a world.
title: Some graphics settings break LOD renderer script logic

comments.body:
LOD0 is not disabled on any quality setting. The "Maximum LOD Level" setting is "0" for all quality settings. The only change to LOD settings between quality levels is the LOD Bias which ranges from 1.0 to 2.0 between Low and Ultra.
Ultra: 2.0
High: 2.0
Medium: 1.5
Low: 1.0
This LOD Bias range was already possible using the built-in Unity settings pop-up that was available by holding Shift while starting the client. Users could select between VRHigh, VRLow, and DesktopLow. VRHigh used an LOD Bias of 2.0 while VRLow and DesktopLow used an LOD Bias of 1.0.
Unity has removed the built-in settings pop-up in Unity 2019 so instead the quality settings have to be available through a VRChat menu option.
The new SDK will populate your project's quality settings to match the VRChat client's quality settings so you can see exactly what settings are used for each quality level by opening the project quality settings from Edit->Project Settings->Quality.

details:
Currently, OnTriggerEnter and friends will trigger collisions for some protected objects - notably, colliders on avatars, but there may be others as well. This is a common point of confusion as your UdonBehaviour may suddenly die when it tries to examine a collider, and you may have difficulty reproducing this (because your avatar doesn't have colliders or triggers on it).
I suspect it's rare to actually need this functionality; while there may be specific use cases that need to detect colliders on avatars, or maybe the quick menu, but for the most part it's just a debugging rabbit hole for Udon beginners. As such, I suggest that Udon filter these events, and guarantee that OnTriggerEnter and friends only be invoked when the collider is not a protected object.
It may be necessary for compatibility to add a flag to retain the old behavior - but the presence of protected colliders is in any case subject to change as VRC's UI changes, or as a player changes avatars, and they can still be potentially found by performing sphere/raycasts, so there are workarounds available for weird usecases.
title: OnTrigger/Collider Enter/Stay/Exit should not fire for protected objects (at least, not by default)

details:
Currently, most assets built with non-graph compilers (i.e. U#) require that the compiler be present, and inject a bunch of C# into your project. This is both a security risk (because you're pulling in editor extensions which can do whatever they like) and a usability issue (you need to pull in a rather large asset, and even if you do want to use U#, your compilation times keep growing as you add assets).
It would be nice to be able to compile this U# code and distribute just the compiled asset. This is _almost_ possible today, but needs a bit more support to be possible without the need for editor scripting to load the compiled code.
In particular, what is needed is a subtype of UdonProgramAsset, distributed as part of the VRCSDK, which:
1. Serializes the program within the ProgramAsset (the current UdonProgramAsset does not do this, and needs to be subclassed to be usable)
2. Hides the default disassembly view in the inspector
3. Provides a public function to set the contents based on an IUdonProgram, or a SerializedUdonProgramAsset.
Today, if you wanted to do this precompiled asset distribution, you'd still need your own subclass of UdonProgramAsset that extracts the serialized program from the source SerializedUdonProgramAsset and shoves it into its own fields, and then loads it back later; editor extensions aren't quite avoidable today.
title: Please provide a way to distribute compiled Udon code

details:
To reproduce:
- Create a behaviour with ExecutionOrder -100000
- Create a child of it with another behaviour with no execution order overrides
- Create a behaviour with ExecutionOrder -100000 and **NO** child objects as a control
- Create a new separate behaviour with ExecutionOrder +100000
- Add a log to Start() to keep track of it
Expected result:
- Behaviours with -100000 to log first
- Behaviours with no override to log second
- Behaviours with +100000 to log third
What actually happens:
- Behaviours with -100000 and **NO** children log first
- Behaviours with no override log second
- Behaviours with +100000 log third
- Behaviours with -100000 **WITH** children log fourth

Repro world: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_f43e6a53-97c2-4a6b-88af-60612f4b3cce

**This also creates another large issue**
If you also try to disable those -100000 objects (with Default children) via the +100000 Start() method - the -100000 behaviour will enter a broken state where it will never initialize or receive any events no matter what.
You can toggle them on and off after - no methods will ever fire

I have created a test world that illustrates the above: https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_06ab5f32-ffbe-44dd-9930-b3b28074fcfd

Checking the logs when loading in - you'll see a bunch of objects logging OnEnable (the ones that report `withChild False`), and a bunch of Default objects which are children of other -100000 objects.
Then they will all get disabled by the +100000 behaviour.
Clicking the sphere enables those -100000 parents, but they never log either Start() or OnEnable
title: [1123] Udon Objects with Udon Children initialize late despite execution order overrides

details:
In some cases, a prefab containing an UdonBehaviour can end up with a null serializedProgramAsset, even though the referenced UdonProgramSource has a serialized program asset associated with it. This then results in a failure to load the program:

```
[<color=yellow>UdonBehaviour</color>] Could not load the program; the UdonBehaviour on 'SpherePrefab(Clone)' will not run.
UnityEngine.Debug:Log (object,UnityEngine.Object)
VRC.Core.Logger:Log (string,int,UnityEngine.Object)
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:InitializeUdonContent () (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:1143)
VRC.Udon.UdonManager:RegisterUdonBehaviour (VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour) (at Assets/Udon/UdonManager.cs:668)
VRC.Udon.Wrapper.Modules.ExternVRCInstantiate:__Instantiate__UnityEngineGameObject__UnityEngineGameObject (VRC.Udon.Common.Interfaces.IUdonHeap,uint[]) (at Assets/Udon/WrapperModules/ExternVRCInstantiate.cs:69)
VRC.Udon.VM.UdonVM:Interpret ()
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:RunProgram (uint) (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:884)
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:RunEvent (string,System.ValueTuple`2<string, object>[]) (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:1066)
VRC.Udon.UdonBehaviour:ManagedUpdate () (at Assets/Udon/UdonBehaviour.cs:447)
VRC.Udon.UdonManager:Update () (at Assets/Udon/UdonManager.cs:251)
```

This issue has cropped up a few times in the wild, and with the help of Haï~ I have a minimal repro procedure (using only Udon Graph, to make sure it's not an U# bug):

1. Create a new project and import VRCSDK3-WORLD-2021.08.11.15.16_Public
2. Import this unitypackage: https://www.dropbox.com/s/572efzuno9xvbbm/fails%20to%20set%20serialized%20program%20source.unitypackage?dl=0
3. Initially, if you enter play mode, you will see two spheres, which both turn green. One is a spawned prefab, one is a prefab instance present from scene load.
4. Delete the SerializedUdonPrograms folder.
5. Enter play mode again. You'll see two spheres, but only one will turn green; the spawned prefab will fail to load its udon program with the stacktrace above.

Once in this state, editing or recompiling the udon program does not fix it; however, it can be fixed by opening and closing the prefab.
I'm pretty sure there are other ways to enter this state than deleting the SerializedUdonPrograms directory, but this is the only consistent repro procedure we've found so far.
title: UdonBehaviours on Prefabs don't set their serializedProgramAsset, resulting in program load failures

details:
Looping over all childs of a transform to find a certain child with a given name is really expensive in Udon. It's what takes one of the biggest performance hits currently in our scripts. You cannot use Transform.Find() in a lot of cases which is the closest Unity function to that.
I noticed that having a native function from VRChat doing this for us would be a good way to increase performance, especially if this search is also done over childs of childs etc., while it's also easily to implement.
Ideally, we would get a GetChildWithName() function that returns the child which has a name that starts with a given string (so instead of String.Equals it uses String.StartsWith()), plus the optional parameter if disabled gameObjects should be included or not, and an optional parameter if this search should only be performed for direct childs or also for childs of childs (all layers down). Furthermore, a function that returns an array of all findings would be great. These functions could be added to the Utilities class for example. 
Note: Transform.Find(), which is the closest Unity function to this, does not perform a recursive descend down a Transform hierarchy, so it does not cover this use case.
title: Please give us a GetChildWithName() function with additional parameters

details:
The new TrackingDataType.Origin should give us the origin of the playspace, which works fine, unless the player enters a station. Then we just get a position reported which has nothing to do with the playspace origin anymore. 
We expect that the distance and offset between origin and head tracking data does not change when entering a station, since it shouldn't be related to that. 
Note: VRChat already sets the origin y to be at ground level, which is already an unexpected behaviour. The offset change when entering a station however is even more unexpected. We need to work out the relative positions from tracking data in the users playspace to get rid of feedback loops that we experience with IK and humanoid bone positions from a player, especially in a station, so a consistent behaviour here is important for us.
Note: This was tested with a custom laying animation. The reported original was suddenly a few centimeters below the head tracking data when being in the station, but fine when not being in the station.
title: TrackingDataType.Origin reports wrong position when player is in a station

details:
We need to know in Udon if someone is using SDK2 or SKD3 avatars and also if they use FBT, e.g. to give them a station which doesn't break their avatar, or to not let them into a specific station and display a message instead. 
Right now, we can either make a station that fully works for SDK3 avatars or for SDK2 avatars. When it comes to FBT users, it get's even more complicated for certain use cases. There are also things that should work differently if the user has full body tracking, not related to stations at all.
"But what are you doing that breaks SDK2/3 avatars?"
We e.g. import parts of the Avatar SDK3 into our SDK3 world unity project to override certain tracking by animation and to adjust the viewpoint. We do this because else the animation / viewpoint only works for SDK2 avatars. Using those components breaks SDK2 avatars. It also breaks some stuff on SDK3 when they exit, like finger tracking, or IK, but the user can at least manually reset their avatar to fix that.
"But wouldn't it be better to fix stations instead?"
We are waiting for working stations since forever and a fix for them usually breaks with the next update. There are so many broken/unexpected behaviour things with stations that we should not wait until an update will fix all issues we are having on our weird use-cases. A lot of people do awesome stuff by using stations in unintended ways or want to tailor something to be used by FBT or a certain avatar version, not only limited to stations.
Note: There is a guide regarding stations where the avatar version can branch in an animator. This is good, but does not cover any use case, especially if you need the information without or before having the user in a station. https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrc_station#sdk3-station-with-sdk2sdk3-avatar

details:
According to a response from Phasedragon on the official discord, putting a UdonBehaviour with None syncmode on a gameobject will break syncing for any other UBs on that gameobject.
When building reusable components, it would be preferable to be able to slap None mode onto any UdonBehaviour that does not, itself, require sync, while still being able to add other UdonBehaviours that need sync. Consider, for example, a simple UdonBehaviour that adds collision sounds to any rigidbody. We should be able to add this regardless of whether the object is synced or not. With the proposed None sync mode behavior, it would be necessary to mark this helper UB as being either continuous or manual sync mode (and it would only be able to coexist with UB of the same type).
If, instead, none sync mode was considered 'weaker' than ObjectSync, Continuous, or Manual modes, and to defer to those modes if a corresponding component was present, we'd have much better composability than the proposed semantics.
title: SyncMode None should be "weaker" than other sync modes

comments.body: Sync mode is a gameobject-wide decision, so you really shouldn't slot together reusable components onto the same gameobject if they have different sync modes. You should have them on separate gameobjects.

@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name}: I'm more asking that reusable UdonBehaviours which don't care about networking, have a way of saying "I don't care about networking; don't initialize it just for my sake, and don't get in the way of anything else on the GameObject that wants to do networking". I don't see a use case for the current ("I actively want networking to break") that isn't covered by the "I don't care" semantics I propose above.
In particular, due to the way unity event routing works, it's often not an option to move things to separate gameobjects (see the collider-to-audio component above - you can't move that to a different GameObject than the collider, and if sometimes you also need Object Sync on that object, you're stuck).
While it's possible to configure on a per-UB basis to get things consistent, that's extra configuration work - with U# the sync mode can be set automatically, removing error-prone manual setup steps, but not if you need to change it each time to match the other UBs.
@{60285ca04963ba22994f485b|full_name} Are there any documentation pages describing the final behavior with conflicting none+other sync modes in the new open beta version?
@{5c1475afb7ce126e9e0e3a39|full_name}: No changes have been made to this behavior in open beta 1132. This is still under review and if anything changes it will be included in the patch notes.
This has been implemented in the 1144 open beta.

comments.body:
World this behaviour can be tested in: https://vrchat.com/i/cloak-disruptxyzzy-2e169
1. After spawning walk to the white cube next to the spawn (near the "tunnel")
2. make sure to stand on the side closer to the spawn to be inside the disabled trigger
3. click the white cube to enable the trigger
4. check the Log for "OnPlayerTriggerEnter" (does not appear currently)
5. click the white cube twice to disable and enable the trigger again
6. in the  Log the "OnPlayerTriggerEnter" should have appeared
(As an alternative to checking the log you can test whether other players that are not in the trigger can not hear you, if it was working you would not be able to hear players not in the trigger and they would not be able to hear you inside the trigger as soon as it becomes visible).
EDIT: I was wrong in my reply here, so removing it to avoid confusing people.

@{5de9405aea7cc52772fcc359|full_name}: Your explanation of OnTriggerEnter is incorrect, but OnTriggerExit is correct. Unity considers enabling a collider or GameObject with a collider as an enter event and will fire OnTriggerEnter for all colliders within the enabled collider.
The bug that Guribo is reporting here is that UdonBehaviours will fail to send OnTriggerEnter events for objects that enter before the Udon program has been initialized. You can easily test this by adding logging within UdonBehaviour.cs. See the attached screenshots. I have added logging to OnEnable, OnDisable, and OnTriggerEnter. I have also created a program that logs inside OnPlayerTriggerEnter. When the object is enabled, you see the OnTriggerEnter method fire before hasDoneStart is set to true, which means that it will be ignored.
For creators, the solution would be to ensure the collider is disabled initially, and enabled in start when you know the program is initialized. This is something creators will have a hard time debugging since it is a bug in Udon and different than expected Unity behavior.

@{5f4c34d0995917085be1218d|full_name}: Oh! Thanks for the correction, and for explaining the issue further. I thought Enter and Stay had the same rules as Exit,   I should have checked the docs before replying here. I'll correct my statement above and look into this issue further.

details:
Some avatars have no head tracking data. It simply returns the world origin.
I had expected to get at least the camera position/rotation.
Test world: https://vrchat.com/i/fusl-pythondeclan-b4cf1
Affacted avatar: https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_ca5c260d-ff81-4b85-b522-1e44dea95770

comments.body:
That is a generic avatar, so there is no need to sync the position of the head. That would be a waste of bandwidth for vrchat to sync it on the off chance that some udon script might need it. The same reasoning applies to the tracking data of a remote player. The same problem occurs for a humanoid avatar that is missing some bones, since some bones are optional. If it is humanoid however, the head is not optional. 
This is a situation where you should probably make your own udon script to sync the values if you want other players to see them.

@{5b7fb61894211b58b866e8ae|full_name}: In that case the API is misleading. "Tracking data" does not suggest any relation to a specific avatar. Also there is no API call that allows checking the type of avatar you are using. You'd need to check for missing bones etc to figure that out. The argument of not syncing the head tracking data when it is generic is also not a very strong argument as you are already saving a lot as there is no humanoid IK that needs to be synced...

Additionally: on avatars simply the bone rotation is returned which in this case is not facing forward but backward, effectively making my script believe Rod is facing away from me when we face each other. I believe the head position/rotation is available under the hood as it might be used for example the player voice position (this is just an assumption) and thus could be exposed as tracking data.
With the current implementation it is difficult to reliably determine the direction a remote player is looking/facing without analysing the bone structure or frequently sending bone-tracking-data offsets just so you can recreate the actual tracking data...

details:
Additional Array methods were added in https://docs.vrchat.com/v2021.4.1/docs/vrchat-202114#changes-improvements-and-fixes-1 with the accompanying canny post marked as complete https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/add-more-array-methods-to-all-array-types but Array.Sort was mysteriously left out.

This would be EXTREMELY useful for quickly making a deterministic list of players using GetPlayers()'s VRCPlayerApi array by playerId (and then sorting the VRCPlayerApis by playerID with Array.Sort(keys, items)).  Currently in Udon that array is out of order for different clients, and individual playerIds represent their join order, rather than an autofilled sequence from players leaving and joining.

It would also be useful for sorting VRCPlayerApis by a world's game score for a scoreboard.  Array.Sort is extremely useful because, even though we don't have access to custom data structures or IComparable implementations in Udon, we can still sort things using associated arrays of intrinsic data types.

And before you do the same thing that you did with the previous post, please just whitelist everything you can.  Not just Array methods.  Stringbuilders.  Native Unity components like LODGroups.  Although a rumor, I heard that ReflectionProbe endpoints weren't included for a YEAR after Udon's release because there was a blacklist for anything with 'reflection' in the name.  Please consider going back through the whitelist and enabled anything and everything possible.
title: Array.Sort

comments.body: Array.Sort has a number of overloads which seem based on looking at the other exposed Array methods to be exposable.  Array.Find only has a couple overload but both seem exposable.  On the same line, Array.Reverse has two typed overloads which aren't exposed.  It could simply be a mistake that none of these are exposed. Sort is very useful since implementing array sorting in Udon is expensive. Fill is along the same lines expensive.

@{5adf7c5544b24b6ef7cb0f25|full_name}: one difficulty with sort is that, since we can't create custom data structures or delegates, you'd only be able to sort primitive ints or strings, which is not as useful as one might hope...
bump

I updated the World SDK to 3.7.1-beta and tried it, but it still doesn't seem to work!

The array used in the error in the image is int[].

Thank you for the request!

We just released this feature in SDK 3.7.1.

https://creators.vrchat.com/releases/release-3-7-1/

@{5e8487f1fd13be66cecc227b|full_name}, does the feature work for you in the final release? Or are you still experiencing issues?

I see.

It is true that Array.Sort() was exposed.

My way of doing it was interpreted as Sort<T[]>(T[]), while Sort<T[]>(T[]) is not exposed in U#, which seems to have caused the compile error.

After upcasting the array as follows, it compiles and works as expected.

  Sort((Array)_trackNumberList);

========= Translate Japanese ============

なるほど。

確かに Array.Sort() はexposeされていました。

私のやり方では Sort<T[]>(T[]) として解釈され、一方 Sort<T[]>(T[]) はU#ではexposeされていない事がコンパイルエラーとなったようです。

次のように配列をアップキャストしたら、コンパイルされて期待通りに動くようになりました。

  System.Array.Sort((Array)_trackNumberList);

@{63691297469f06772579fe6f|full_name} The implementation of this as it currently exists in the SDK is not particularly useful. As @{5e8487f1fd13be66cecc227b|full_name} said, the most common way to use this is `Sort<T[]>(T[])` and specifically `Sort<T[]>(T[], Comparison<T>)` which allows us to sort arrays of a specific type by properties of that type.

For anyone who may read this and need to use Array.Sort(), you'll need to cast your arrays as the Array type. So for example if you have an variable int[] nameOfArray, you'll need to do Array.Sort((Array)nameOfArray) to sort it, otherwise Udon will say it's not exposed if you attempt to work on it as an int[] directly.

comments.body:
Follow up: According to my testing, Network.SetOwner blocks completely until either both parts of OnOwnershipRequest return true and all execution inside OnOwnershipTransferred is resolved OR when part 1 or 2 of OnOwnershipRequest returns false and the transfer is canceled.  Therefore, checking gameObject owner right after Network.SetOwner will indicate success or failure of the transfer.
The documentation explains that you should be able to safely call Network.SetOwner, change synced variables,  and call RequestSerialization in order and things should sync, but it doesn't explain by what mechanism it ensures that this works.  It would be nice for the docs to be updated with the information on the above process if it is correct.

Upon further testing, changing synced variables directly after Network.SetOwner or inside OnOwnershipTransferred is NOT safe.  As of build 1144, some players will receive serialized data from the new owner BEFORE they receive the ownership transfer and discard it.  
This behavior is antithetical to manual sync, as the synced data will need to be periodically re-serialized to ensure its delivered.  Alternatively, every other player could use individually owned synced variables as semaphores to let a new owner know when they've all received ownership transfer and sync is reliable.  Both ways are dirty, and Udon networking should be changed to ensure that serialized data is received or at least processed after all ownership transfers for that object have been received.
Possibly related to https://feedback.vrchat.com/udon-networking-update/p/1097-ownership-desync-issue
https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/setting-ownership-to-someone-else-in-the-same-tick-as-requestserialization-cause

details:
StaticBatchingUtility.Combine sets up static batching for several objects at runtime. It offers the following advantages over marking objects as batching static in the editor:
-Allows the performance advantages of static batching to be applied to objects generated at runtime. Since such objects don't exist in the editor, it's not possible to mark them as batching static. 
-Objects setup to be statically batched in this way can be moved by adjusting the transform of their associated staticBatchingRoot gameobject. This is useful for sets of objects that move together as a whole.
For these reasons exposing StaticBatchingUtility.Combine would provide world creators with a useful tool for optimizing their worlds.
https://docs.unity3d.com/2019.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/StaticBatchingUtility.html
title: Expose StaticBatchingUtility.Combine

You can connect a input port typed `Component` to a output port typed `UdonBehaviour` (see attached 1st image). But it's impossible to connect them in inverted direction (2nd image). That is dragging from output port to input port.

otherType == typeof(IUdonEventReceiver) && type == typeof(Component)

details:
Requesting serialization on an object and immediately disabling it prevents the serialization request.
Setup:
- Manually synched object with several synched variables
- Remote player is owner
- Remove player leaves instance
- Master takes ownership
- Master resets various variables and requests serialization
- Master disables `GameObject`
**Expected:** Serialization succeeds (This is what happened before the OSC update)
**Actual:** `OnPreSerialization` and `OnPostSerialization` are **not** called, the variables are not reset. 
-------------
Since the OSC update, there seems to be a new issue when requesting serialization.
I have only seen this bug occur in CyanLaser's object pool prefab. It is caused by disabling an object shortly after requesting serialization. 
If I don't disable the `GameObject`, serilization succeeds (but the script loses functionality)
https://github.com/CyanLaser/CyanPlayerObjectPool/blob/main/Cyan/PlayerObjectPool/UdonSharp/CyanPlayerObjectAssigner.cs#L676
title: [11694] Networking bug: Serialization fails unexpected when object is disabled

comments.body:
Because this was not mentioned in the patch notes I submitted this as a bug. Either way, I'd appreciate if this was looked into, as I heavily rely on the behaviour that was present before the OSC patch.
Oh, and apologies for the typo in the title. I'd edit it if I could! 😁

I can reproduce the issue in Super VR Ball 95% of the time (not sure what's up with the other 5% though!)
- Object pool has 2 objects.
- 2 players, master and clientm, start a game and join the race
- Remote client reconnects.
- Remote client is immediately in the race, on a ball, when the ball should have been reset.
This currently happens in all public instances of Super VR Ball as well. The object pool is larger, so it's random whether a player gets assigned a `GameObject` that wasn't reset properly.
After further testing, this also seems to happen when enabling GameObjects. After enabling a previously disabled GameObject we *may* also need to wait. Otherwise RequestSerialization fails.

I've been able to circumvent the issue by implement a queue system that disables objects after a one second delay.
This, uh, makes me more confident that the behaviour described is a bug, and not an intentional change.
Related: https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/1171-deserialization-fires-for-owner-and-serialized-data-is-overridden-by-old-da

Technically, this will be improved in a later update that we're working on so I will mark this as in progress. However, I should mention that you should never rely on every serialization to happen exactly once or even for every serialization to happen at all. It is not a messaging system, it is a syncing system. You may receive the same data twice or you might not receive some intermediate values at all. What matters is that everyone is "eventually consistent" and lands on the same value after the dust settles.
You are welcome to add your own logic on top of this to create a messaging system, such as a timestamp to ignore repeated messages or an array of values to queue up and send multiple quick messages at once.

Well, we've been working on this for a long time now - about 10 months. And I'm happy to say that the update fixing this issue has now been released to open beta! Users joining the instance will no longer cause the owner to resend all their data and get everybody clogged in extreme cases.

details:
Please expose layout based key checks so creators can provide better user experience in worlds.
Unity's input system has methods for checking keyboard keys based on the location of the keyboard rather than the specific letter. VRChat has a global player base which means users can have any possible keyboard layout. Most world creators assume the user will have the qwerty keyboard layout, but any other layout may cause issues with the selected input key checks. World creators currently have no way to resolve this. 
As an example, the French keyboard layout swaps the A and Q keys from the qwerty layout. This means that using the Q key would always fire when the user tries to move left. The Q key is near the wasd movement keys and seems like a good option, but creates a bad experience for users using the French keyboard layout.
title: Expose Keyboard location based input keys

details:
Previously exposed TMP methods are not exposed any longer (or maybe never really were).
For instance, `ForceMeshUpdate` was exposed in update 2021.4.1 (https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/vrchat-202141)
for both `TextMeshPro` and `TextMeshProUGUI` but is *unavailable* for `TextMeshPro`.
Note the difference that `TextMeshProUGUI` is for canvases and `TextMeshPro` for being placed inside the scene.
Another issue is being `TMP_CharacterInfo[]` exposed (via `TextMeshProUGUI.characterInfo`) but the type itself, 
`TMP_CharacterInfo`, is unexposed.
Therefore I request to reiterate over this list and expose what's unexposed:
- `TextMeshPro.textInfo`
- `TextMeshPro.meshInfo`
- `TextMeshPro.mesh`
- `TextMeshPro.enabled`
- `TextMeshPro.ForceMeshUpdate`
- `TextMeshPro.UpdateGeometry`

- `TextMeshProUGUI.textInfo`
- `TextMeshProUGUI.meshInfo`
- `TextMeshProUGUI.mesh`
- `TextMeshProUGUI.enabled`
- `TextMeshProUGUI.ForceMeshUpdate`
- `TextMeshProUGUI.UpdateGeometry`

Overall, all methods and fields by these two main types should be evaluated for being exposed, including base members.
However without these following types doing anything but basic operations on TMP is pretty much pointless, hence I request these types (not only as array) to be exposed, including their fields and methods: 
- `TMP_MeshInfo`
- `TMP_TextInfo`
- `TMP_CharacterInfo`
- `TMP_ColorGradient`
- `TMP_Text`
- `TMP_Dropdown`

The first two images in the attachment show how the same method is not exposed for different TMP types.
The third image is displaying how a variety of types are exposed as array only. 
The fourth image showcases how `TextMeshPro` is also mostly unexposed, the list grows even longer when including base members.
In contrast, the fifth image presents `TextMeshProUGUI` (without base members).
It will be amazing if this is being looked into because TMP is a very powerful tool. 
Thank you for your time!

details:
If we had a JUMP_IF_ZERO  and JUMP_IF_NULL equivalent of the existing JUMP_IF_FALSE we could save on extern calls for many sanity checks and logic paths.
I do many == null sanity checks in code for validating whether an object exists or not. With a JUMP_IF_NULL op, code could be compiled such that the Equality extern is no longer needed thus making the udon script run faster.
Similarly JUMP_IF_ZERO would be great to have for validating against numerical default values (which are always initialized as zero).
title: Please add new JUMP_IF_ZERO and JUMP_IF_NULL UASM operations

comments.body: I'm not entirely sure how much of a performance benefit this would provide for null checks and I would need to profile it. Similar for JUMP_IF_ZERO. The tradeoff for both is that they need to determine the type they are comparing; `int` comparison is not the same as `float` comparison, and similarly`System.Object` comparison is not the same as `UnityEngine.Object` comparison. So to avoid overhead of checking the argument types they'd each need to be split off into their own instructions. Externs have the benefit in a way that they already have the exact comparison op they need.

So basically a suite of numerical comparison operations, paired with types
{beq,bne,blt,bge}{fi} + {beq,bne}{U,O} - or some subset thereof*.
* branch if equal/branch if not equal/branch if less than/branch if greater than or equal
It might be worth either examining the UASM output of commonplace/popular prefabs (anyone could do this), and counting the number of equality extern calls to estimate the impact of such instructions.
This would somewhat resemble a move from RISC to CISC, but given that the Udon VM is a straight-up interpreter and not a JIT it sort of makes sense to ahead-of-time optimize with specialized instructions.

@{61898ae3ee3a174b8e9086e5|full_name}: Fair enough.
What if the ops were combined into a JUMP_IF_INEQUAL? would the == operation be a valid case for moving into UASM land? For the UnityEngine.Object, it's already recommended to use the Utilities.IsValid anyways, so the JUMP_IF_FALSE op would apply for that one.

@{5f6be62b15f9fa5364f1834c|full_name}: It's the same kind of situation, you're paying a cost that will possibly be worse overall to just determine the type of equality/inequality you need to do. Alternatively it's calling .Equals() internally which results in boxing which could also turn out worse because Unity's allocator is bad.
I also wouldn't recommend using Utilities.IsValid if you know you're dealing with a UnityEngine.Object in U#. It's more of a primitive to simplify graphs.
Adding ops for common things like this is something that may happen, but it's a less clear-cut improvement and could end up slowing down the interpreter loop overall more than it helps depending on how poor IL2CPP and such is about it. So it needs a fair amount of evaluation and I think there are other areas that are more likely to have a larger impact that would probably be explored first.

This was talked about a bit in #udon-questions
Rather than exposing a Player Transform directly (which can lead to security issues)
I purpose a wrapped class that stores the reference to the Transform (but doesn't expose it) and only exposes the non-destructive parts of Transform to the end user.
Essentially TrackingData except extended to allow for more than just Head and Hands and allows usage of methods such as TransformPoint, InverseTransformPoint, TransformDirection, etc.
Wrapper methods within the wrapped class could be restricted for security purposes and developers could use Transform methods in a secure manner right off the wrapped class instance.
The main difference between this and what Udon does now is being able to access methods that are otherwise not exposed and the VRChat developers still being able to maintain security over those exposed methods.
For example lets call our wrapped class WrappedTransform.
The instance of WrappedTransform wouldn't be passible to Object.Destroy but a world developer could still use something like WrappedTransform.InverseTransformPoint if they wanted.
title: Expose a Wrapped Class for Restricted Object Transforms

details:
Whilst the addition of Copy/Paste to the keyboard is welcome in [1220], there may be times when a world developer wishes to initiate a copy for text data via udon.
 —
# Examples
1. A world developer has user persistent data. They wish for the user to save this user persistent data without potential for error, such as deletion of text using the on-screen keyboard. As such, they provide a "Copy" button, that when pressed, writes to the clipboard, allowing the user to paste the data elsewhere for storage.
2. A user has a video player. However, they wish to improve Quest compatibility by providing a "URL converter" that takes popular media links and converts them to a link-resolver equivalent, as is common. Rather than risk the user accidentally back-spacing portions of the URL which they cannot see within the VRCHAT keyboard, they intelligently convert and copy the new URL `on End Edit`, for the user to paste into a video player address bar.
3. A world developer is hosting an event. During this event, they wish to provide codes which are linked to a website for various event-related activities or interactions. Rather than force the user to exit VRChat unnecessarily by way of URL, they provide a menu in-world to copy the code(s) at any time, which can be pasted into a website at a later time.
 —
# Request
Please add support for the [GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer](https://docs.unity3d.com/2019.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/GUIUtility-systemCopyBuffer.html), by adding a `GUIUtility set systemCopyBuffer` node, and write-only access to `GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer` in U#.
 —
# Why Write-Only
Being aware of VRChat's concerns with general purpose input/output (GPIO) from the VRC client, write-only access would require user-intervention to write back ("paste") clipboard contents in any particular world, and would be restricted to doing so in UI Input Fields and *re-implementations* thereof.
 
**Likewise**, write only access **prevents random-access of the user clipboard**, *which poses a security risk in the event the clipboard contains sensitive content.*
 —
# Further considerations
**If random-write access is of a concern, the Udon implementation could provide a mandatory UI dialog prompting the user if they wish to to copy text to the clipboard.**
E.G. "*Do you wish to copy "Some random text that will be truncated..." [509 Characters] to the clipboard?*" with "`Cancel`" & "`Copy`" options.
**Likewise, a variable indicating the copy's success could be provided, allowing udon developers to handle copy failure.**
E.G. `GUIUtility set systemCopyBuffer` will return a bool indicating the success (true) or failure (false) based on whether the user copied or canceled the action.
title: Add Write-Only Access to Clipboard (systemCopyBuffer)

details:
As it stands, the ability for developers to apply occlusion culling to udon scripts themselves is fairly limited. There are many cases where behaviors, such as those ran in `Update`/`LateUpdate`/`FixedUpdate`, **are not necessary when the objects attached are not in view**.
 —
# Example
A developer adds a "scrubber" to a video player, with time display via text on both sides. Once per second (done by collecting the `time` during each `LateUpdate` and comparing it to a copy of the time stored during the last update), the udon behavior pulls the current time of the video, the length of the video, applies these to the scrubber, then runs a series of floors and multiplication & division to the time and max time before formatting them into a string for a HH:MM:SS time display.
The entirety of this behavior is only necessary when the controls are actively within view of the player, and could be safely culled.
Another developer has a game world. They are looking for a way to have an NPC move and act when the viewer is not facing the NPC. By providing the option to register the NPC's visibility, when the player looks away (and no camera is in view) the NPC's specified udon behaviors will engage, until such a time that the player or a camera looks at them again.
 —
# Request
Add support for the [OnBecameInvisible](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnBecameInvisible.html) & [OnBecameVisible](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnBecameVisible.html) events.
 —
# Additional Note
In reading, for some there is confusion with these events, as Unity's behavior **purportedly includes Editor views, including the Scene view, even when inactive, in determining visibility.** If true, documentation should note that for successful testing in-editor, the scene view should be pointed **away** from the object which behavior is being tested.
 —
# Related Feedback
- [OnBecameInvisible, OnBecameVisible, broken](https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/onbecameinvisible-onbecamevisible-broken)
title: Add support for OnBecameVisible & OnBecameInvisible

comments.body: Ran into the same issue with GetBonePosition(HumanBodyBones.LeftHand) or GetBonePosition(HumanBodyBones.RightHand). Works, after code runs in Update method instead of LateUpdate method.
Recent project of mine where i ran into this same thing.

FYI, this bug report here is missing some crucial details (the issue is the bone data, not tracking data, and this affects more than just LateUpdate). It is also not a bug, as far as I understand it. 

First of all, remote players don't have tracking data, they will always return the hand bone data instead. The reason for this is that tracking data isn't sent over network. 

But most importantly, the issue is that Udon doesn't cache bone positions, instead they give you direct access to the armature at any given time, which is a problem because this armature is probably moving around due to IK calculations before settling at the final position. You can only access the correct data in PostLateUpdate() as far as my testing has gone.

The solution for this would be to not give Udon direct access to bone data, but to cache the correct data after each finished IK calculation. Here is my canny for that: https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/always-provide-correct-bone-data

@{5f2eaed841e042066f65cb45|full_name}: If you need the correct bone data, you need to use PostLateUpdate() instead. Update() will only give you outdated information. It probably doesn't matter for your use case, because it will be close enough, but there is a visible lag behind the real position when using Update() instead of PostLateUpdate().
@{5f3287055bc2dc276e0f1630|full_name}: Thank you. In meantime it is also documented somewhere in the VRC docs (maybe also before, but I didn't check). Using PostLateUpdate solved my problem.

@{5f2eaed841e042066f65cb45|full_name}: Unfortunately there are a few cases where this isn't helping. In particular because you cannot control during which timing certain events are being called, e.g. networking events or player interactions. And PostLateUpdate isn't available for delayed events (who knows why). But you can help upvoting the following canny if you want it to be fixed for all use cases, because the fix would be rather trivial:  https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/always-provide-correct-bone-data

details:
The VRC team has suggested that it might offer a consent-based solution for allowing Worlds to override Earmuff Mode: https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/1220-earmuff-mode-should-be-overwritten-by-custom-udon-not-the-other-way-around
Please extend that solution to include any important user settings that intersect with World experience.
World creators are using VRChat to pioneer new applications of VR like games, theater, and live-action roleplaying. Such uses require the World creator to have enough control to guarantee that users are having a well-designed experience.
Currently, key elements of World experience are completely out of control of creators. Users should retain final control over most of these settings for safety and accessibility reasons, but World creators need better tools for guiding users for the best experience in their World.
I suggest a prompt upon joining a World (default disabled in the SDK) that advises the user of the best settings for the World, formatted as an approval dialogue so that users don't need to navigate their menu. This is analogous to how web browsers and phone apps will request certain permissions in context, via prompt.
The world's requested settings should automatically revert to the user's previous settings upon leaving the world.
The included image shows an example. World creators could include some or all of these requests, or others.
I invite others to comment below with other settings that might be good to be requestable by a world creator. For now, I think the three most important are:
- World volume level. Hard cap this request to 70%.
- Earmuff mode off
- Nameplates On or Off
title: Allow Worlds to request important settings configurations

comments.body:
Other notes:
- default this feature off in the SDK; creators should only hit users with prompts if they know they need it
- the prompt should not appear if settings are already in alignment with world requests
- the volume slider should have a "tolerance" range that won't prompt so long as user's setting is near enough to requested
- volume slider request should let the world creator specify "at least" and/or "at most"

Fax brought to my attention that the suggestion to hard cap a volume slider at 70% might be too low because of this functionality:
https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/audio-controls-reduce-volume-2x-more-quickly-than-they-should
I agree generally. 70% is just a number I made up anyway.
But in general there should be a hard cap; world creators shouldn't be able to nudge users to set their volume to 100%, because that's completely unnecessary and invites abuse.
And in any case, that point is not a central detail to this request. The main request is the ability to prompt for a volume setting in the first place.
